children.text: 1. Khaṇḍa: Dīkṣā-vidhi
children.translated_text: 1. Section: The Procedure of Initiation (<s>Dīkṣā-vidhi</s>)

children.text: athâto dīkṣāṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ || Parks_1.1 ||
children.translated_text: Now, therefore, we shall explain <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation). [Parks 1.1]

children.text: bhagavān parama-śiva-bhaṭṭārakaḥ śruty-ādy-aṣṭādaśa-vidyāḥ sarvāṇi darśanāni līlayā tat-tad-avasthā-''pannaḥ praṇīya, saṃvinmayyā bhagavatyā bhairavyā svâtmâbhinnayā pṛṣṭaḥ pañcabhiḥ mukhaiḥ pañcâmnāyān paramârtha-sāra-bhūtān praṇināya || Parks_1.2 ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One, the supreme Lord <s>Paramaśiva Bhaṭṭāraka</s>, having playfully composed the eighteen sciences beginning with the <s>Śruti</s> (Vedas) and all the philosophical systems, assuming various states for each, when questioned by the blessed Goddess <s>Bhairavī</s>, who is of the nature of consciousness (<s>saṃvinmayī</s>) and non-different from his own self, proclaimed through his five mouths the five <s>āmnāyas</s> (traditions), which are the essence of the supreme truth. [Parks 1.2]

children.text: tatrâyaṃ siddhāntaḥ || Parks_1.3 ||
children.translated_text: Herein is the established doctrine (<s>siddhānta</s>). [Parks 1.3]

children.text: ṣaṭtriṃśat-tattvāni viśvam || Parks_1.4 ||
children.translated_text: The thirty-six <s>tattvas</s> (principles) constitute the universe. [Parks 1.4]

children.text: śarīra-kañcukitaḥ śivo jīvo niṣkañcukaḥ para-śivaḥ || Parks_1.5 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s> encased in the body-sheaths is the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>); without the sheaths, he is <s>Paraśiva</s> (the supreme <s>Śiva</s>). [Parks 1.5]

children.text: sva-vimarśaḥ purusârthaḥ || Parks_1.6 ||
children.translated_text: Self-awareness (<s>svavimarśa</s>) is the goal of human life (<s>puruṣārtha</s>). [Parks 1.6]

children.text: varṇâtmakā nityāḥ śabdāḥ || Parks_1.7 ||
children.translated_text: Sounds, being of the nature of <s>varṇas</s> (phonemes), are eternal. [Parks 1.7]

children.text: mantrāṇām acintya-śaktitā || Parks_1.8 ||
children.translated_text: The power of <s>mantras</s> is inconceivable. [Parks 1.8]

children.text: saṃpradāya-viśvāsābhyāṃ sarva-siddhiḥ || Parks_1.9 ||
children.translated_text: All <s>siddhis</s> (accomplishments) come from tradition (<s>saṃpradāya</s>) and faith (<s>viśvāsa</s>). [Parks 1.9]

children.text: viśvāsa-bhūyiṣṭhaṃ prāmāṇyam || Parks_1.10 ||
children.translated_text: Validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) is primarily based on faith. [Parks 1.10]

children.text: guru-mantra-devatā-''tma-manaḥ-pavanānām
children.translated_text: From the unification and fruition of the guru, <s>mantra</s>, deity (<s>devatā</s>), self (<s>ātman</s>), mind (<s>manas</s>), and breath (<s>pavana</s>),

children.text: aikya--niṣphālanād antarātma--vittiḥ || Parks_1.11 ||
children.translated_text: the inner self is realized (<s>antarātmavittiḥ</s>). [Parks 1.11]

children.text: ānandaṃ brahmaṇo rūpaṃ, tac ca dehe vyavasthitaṃ, tasyâbhivyañjakāḥ pañca ma-kārāḥ, tair arcanaṃ guptyā, prākaṭyān nirayaḥ || Parks_1.12 ||
children.translated_text: Bliss (<s>ānanda</s>) is the form of <s>Brahman</s>, and it is established in the body. The five <s>makāras</s> are its revealers. Worship should be performed with them in secrecy; from public disclosure comes hell. [Parks 1.12]

children.text: bhāvanā-dārḍhyād ājñā-siddhiḥ || Parks_1.13 ||
children.translated_text: From the firmness of meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>), the power of command (<s>ājñāsiddhi</s>) is attained. [Parks 1.13]

children.text: sarva-darśanânindā || Parks_1.14 ||
children.translated_text: There should be no disparagement of any philosophical system. [Parks 1.14]

children.text: agaṇanaṃ kasyâpi || Parks_1.15 ||
children.translated_text: One should not look down upon anyone. [Parks 1.15]

children.text: sac-chiṣye rahasya-kathanam || Parks_1.16 ||
children.translated_text: The secret teaching should be imparted only to a worthy disciple. [Parks 1.16]

children.text: sadā vidyā-'nusaṃhatiḥ || Parks_1.17 ||
children.translated_text: One should always maintain continuity with the <s>vidyā</s> (sacred knowledge). [Parks 1.17]

children.text: satataṃ śivatā-samāveśaḥ || Parks_1.18 ||
children.translated_text: One should constantly immerse oneself in the state of <s>Śiva</s> (<s>śivatāsamāveśa</s>). [Parks 1.18]

children.text: kāma-krodha-lobha-moha-mada-mātsaryâvihita-hiṃsā-steya-loka-vidviṣṭa-varjanam || Parks_1.19 ||
children.translated_text: One should avoid desire (<s>kāma</s>), anger (<s>krodha</s>), greed (<s>lobha</s>), delusion (<s>moha</s>), intoxication (<s>mada</s>), jealousy (<s>mātsarya</s>), unauthorized violence (<s>hiṃsā</s>), theft (<s>steya</s>), and what is despised by the world. [Parks 1.19]

children.text: eka-gurûpāstir asaṃśayaḥ || Parks_1.20 ||
children.translated_text: Devotion to a single guru, free from doubt. [Parks 1.20]

children.text: sarvatra niṣparigrahatā || Parks_1.21 ||
children.translated_text: Non-possessiveness (<s>niṣparigrahatā</s>) in all things. [Parks 1.21]

children.text: phalaṃ tyaktvā karma--karaṇam || Parks_1.22 ||
children.translated_text: Performing action while renouncing the fruit. [Parks 1.22]

children.text: anitya-karma-lopaḥ || Parks_1.23 ||
children.translated_text: The cessation of non-eternal <s>karmas</s>. [Parks 1.23]

children.text: ma-pañcakâlābhe 'pi nitya-krama-pratyavamṛṣṭiḥ || Parks_1.24 ||
children.translated_text: Even when the five <s>makāras</s> are unavailable, one should reflect upon the eternal procedure (<s>nityakrama</s>). [Parks 1.24]

children.text: nirbhayatā sarvatra || Parks_1.25 ||
children.translated_text: Fearlessness in all situations. [Parks 1.25]

children.text: sarvaṃ vedyaṃ havyam indriyāṇi srucaḥ śaktayo jvālāḥ svâtmā śivaḥ pāvakaḥ svayam eva hotā || Parks_1.26 ||
children.translated_text: All that is knowable is the oblation (<s>havya</s>); the senses are the sacrificial ladles (<s>sruc</s>); the powers (<s>śaktis</s>) are the flames; one's own self is <s>Śiva</s>, the fire; and one is oneself the sacrificer (<s>hotṛ</s>). [Parks 1.26]

children.text: nirviṣaya-cid-vimṛṣṭiḥ phalam || Parks_1.27 ||
children.translated_text: The reflection of pure consciousness free from objects is the fruit. [Parks 1.27]

children.text: ātma-lābhān na paraṃ vidyate || Parks_1.28 ||
children.translated_text: There is nothing greater than the attainment of the Self (<s>ātmalābha</s>). [Parks 1.28]

children.text: saiṣā śāstra-śailī || Parks_1.29 ||
children.translated_text: Such is the style of the <s>śāstra</s> (scripture). [Parks 1.29]

children.text: veśyā iva prakaṭā vedâdi-vidyāḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>Vedas</s> and other sciences are like courtesans — displayed openly to all.

children.text: sarveṣu darśaneṣu gupteyaṃ vidyā || Parks_1.30 ||
children.translated_text: This <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) is hidden in all philosophical systems. [Parks 1.30]

children.text: tatra sarvathā matimān dīkṣeta || Parks_1.31 ||
children.translated_text: Therein, the intelligent one should by all means seek initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>). [Parks 1.31]

children.text: dīkṣās tisraḥ śāktī śāmbhavī māntrī ceti |
children.translated_text: There are three kinds of initiation: <s>Śāktī</s>, <s>Śāmbhavī</s>, and <s>Māntrī</s>.

children.text: tatra śāktī śakti-praveśanāt śāmbhavī caraṇa-vinyāsāt
children.translated_text: Of these, <s>Śāktī</s> is through the descent of <s>śakti</s> (power); <s>Śāmbhavī</s> is through the placing of the guru's feet;

children.text: māntrī mantropadiṣṭayā sarvāś ca kuryāt || Parks_1.32 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Māntrī</s> is through the instruction of <s>mantras</s>. One should perform all three. [Parks 1.32]

children.text: ekaikāṃ vety eke || Parks_1.33 ||
children.translated_text: Or only one of them — so say some. [Parks 1.33]

children.text: sad-guruḥ kramaṃ pravartya sāṅgaṃ hutvā taruṇollāsavān śiṣyam āhūya vāsasā mukhaṃ baddhvā gaṇapati-lalitā-śyāmā-vārtālī-parā-pātra-bindubhis tam avokṣya siddhāntaṃ śrāvayitvā || Parks_1.34 ||
children.translated_text: The true guru (<s>sadguru</s>), having set the procedure in motion, having performed the <s>homa</s> (fire offering) with its subsidiary rites, summons the disciple who is radiant with youthful vitality, binds his face with a cloth, sprinkles him with the <s>bindus</s> (seed-syllables) of <s>Gaṇapati</s>, <s>Lalitā</s>, <s>Śyāmā</s>, <s>Vārtālī</s>, and <s>Parā</s>, and makes him hear the established doctrine (<s>siddhānta</s>). [Parks 1.34]

children.text: tac-chirasi rakta-śukla-caraṇaṃ bhāvayitvā tad-amṛta-kṣālitaṃ sarva-śarīram alaṅkuryāt || Parks_1.35 ||
children.translated_text: Having meditated upon the red and white feet on the disciple's head, he should adorn the entire body, washed by that nectar. [Parks 1.35]

children.text: tasyâmūlam ābrahma-bilaṃ prajvalantīṃ prakāśa-laharīṃ jvalad-anala-nibhāṃ dhyātvā tad-raśmibhis tasya pāpa-pāśān dagdhvā || Parks_1.36 ||
children.translated_text: Having meditated upon a blazing wave of light, resembling a blazing fire, extending from the root (<s>mūlādhāra</s>) to the <s>brahmarandhra</s>, and having burned the bonds of sin of the disciple with those rays, [Parks 1.36]

children.text: tri-kaṭu-tri-phalā-catur-jāta-takkola-madayantī-sahadevī-dūrvā-bhasma-mṛttikā-candana-kuṅkuma-rocanā-karpūra-vāsita-jala-pūrṇaṃ vastra-yuga-veṣṭitaṃ nūtana-kalaśaṃ bālā-ṣaḍ-aṅgenâbhyarcya śrī-śyāmā-vārtālī-cakrāṇi nikṣipya tisṛṇām āvaraṇa-mantrair abhyarcya saṃrakṣyâstreṇa pradarśya dhenu-yonī || Parks_1.37 ||
children.translated_text: he should worship a new pot (<s>kalaśa</s>) — filled with water perfumed with the three pungents (<s>trikaṭu</s>), three fruits (<s>triphala</s>), four spices (<s>caturjāta</s>), <s>takkola</s>, <s>madayantī</s>, <s>sahadevī</s>, <s>dūrvā</s> grass, ash, clay, sandalwood, saffron (<s>kuṅkuma</s>), <s>rocanā</s>, and camphor — wrapped with a pair of cloths, worshipping it with the <s>Bālā</s> <s>mantra</s> and its six limbs, placing the <s>cakras</s> (diagrams) of the glorious <s>Śyāmā</s> and <s>Vārtālī</s>, worshipping with the encircling <s>mantras</s> of the three [goddesses], protecting with the <s>astra</s> (weapon <s>mantra</s>), and showing the <s>dhenu</s> and <s>yoni</s> <s>mudrās</s>. [Parks 1.37]

children.text: śiva-yuk-sau-varṇa-karṇike svara-dvandva-juṣṭa-kiñjalkâṣṭake ka ca ṭa ta pa ya śa lâkṣara-vargâṣṭa-yuktâṣṭa-dale dig-aṣṭaka-sthita ṭhaṃ vaṃ catur-aśre mātṛkā-yantre śiṣyaṃ niveśya tena kumbhâmbhasā tisṛbhiḥ vidyābhiḥ snapayet || Parks_1.38 ||
children.translated_text: Having seated the disciple upon the <s>mātṛkāyantra</s> (diagram of the mother-letters) — with <s>Śiva</s> in a golden pericarp embellished with vowel-pairs, with eight petals bearing the eight groups of consonants beginning with <s>ka</s>, <s>ca</s>, <s>ṭa</s>, <s>ta</s>, <s>pa</s>, <s>ya</s>, <s>śa</s>, <s>la</s>, stationed in the eight directions with <s>ṭhaṃ</s> and <s>vaṃ</s>, in a square — he should bathe the disciple with the water of the pot using the three <s>vidyās</s> (sacred formulas). [Parks 1.38]

children.text: sa-dukūlaṃ sâlepaṃ sâbharaṇaṃ sa-mālaṃ suprasannaṃ śiṣyaṃ pārśve niveśya mātṛkāṃ tad-aṅge vinyasya vimukta-mukha-karpaṭasya tasya haste trīn prathama-siktān candanokṣitān dvitīya-khaṇḍān puṣpa-khaṇḍān nikṣipya tattva-mantrair grāsayitvā dakṣiṇa-karṇe bālam upadiśya paścād iṣṭa-manuṃ vadet || Parks_1.39 ||
children.translated_text: Having seated the disciple — wearing fine silk, anointed with paste, adorned with ornaments and garlands, with serene countenance — at his side, having placed the <s>mātṛkā</s> (mother-letters) on his limbs, and having removed the face-cloth, placing in his hands three portions first sprinkled and anointed with sandalwood, and portions of the second section and flower-portions, having made him consume them with the <s>tattva-mantras</s>, he should whisper the <s>Bālā</s> (<s>mantra</s>) in his right ear, and afterward impart the chosen <s>mantra</s>. [Parks 1.39]

children.text: tatas tasya śirasi sva-caraṇaṃ nikṣipya sarvān mantrān sakṛd vā krameṇa vā yathā-'dhikāram upadiśya svâṅgeṣu kim-apy aṅgaṃ śiṣyaṃ sparśayitvā tad-aṅga-mātṛkā-varṇâdi dvy-akṣaraṃ try-akṣaraṃ catur-akṣaraṃ vā ānanda-nātha--śabdântaṃ tasya nāma diśet || Parks_1.40 ||
children.translated_text: Then, placing his own foot upon the disciple's head, having imparted all the <s>mantras</s> either at once or in sequence according to qualification, having the disciple touch some limb of his own body, he should give the disciple a name consisting of two, three, or four syllables from the <s>mātṛkā-varṇa</s> (mother-letters) of that limb, ending with the word '<s>Ānandanātha</s>.' [Parks 1.40]

children.text: bālopadiṣṭeḥ pūrvam ātmanaḥ pādukāṃ ṣaṭ-tāra-yuktāṃ dadyāt || Parks_1.41 ||
children.translated_text: Before imparting the <s>Bālā</s> (<s>mantra</s>), he should give the <s>pādukā</s> (foot-sandal <s>mantra</s>) of himself, joined with the six <s>tāras</s>. [Parks 1.41]

children.text: ācārān anuśiṣya, hārda-caitanyam āmṛśya, vidyā-trayeṇa tad-aṅgaṃ triḥ parimṛjya parirabhya mūrdhany avaghrāya svâtma-rūpaṃ kuryāt || Parks_1.42 ||
children.translated_text: Having instructed in the observances (<s>ācāras</s>), having touched the consciousness of the heart, having wiped his limbs thrice with the three <s>vidyās</s>, embracing him, smelling the crown of his head, he should make him his own form. [Parks 1.42]

children.text: śiṣyo 'pi pūrṇatāṃ bhāvayitvā kṛtârthas taṃ guruṃ yathā-śakti vittair upacarya vidita-veditavyo 'śeṣa-mantrâdhikārī bhaved iti śivam || Parks_1.43 ||
children.translated_text: The disciple too, having meditated on his own completeness (<s>pūrṇatā</s>), fulfilled, should serve that guru according to his ability with wealth. Having come to know all that is to be known, he becomes qualified for all <s>mantras</s> — thus is auspiciousness. [Parks 1.43]

children.text: 2. Khaṇḍa: Gaṇanāyaka-paddhati
children.translated_text: 2. Section: The Procedure of <s>Gaṇanāyaka</s> (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>)

children.text: itthaṃ sad-guror āhita-dīkṣaḥ mahā-vidyā-''rādhana-pratyūhâpohāya gāṇanāyakīṃ paddhatim āmṛśet || Parks_2.1 ||
children.translated_text: Thus, having received initiation from the true guru (<s>sadguru</s>), one should take up the procedure of <s>Gaṇanāyaka</s> (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>) for removing obstacles to the worship of the great <s>vidyā</s> (sacred knowledge). [Parks 2.1]

children.text: brāhme muhūrta utthāya dvādaśânte sahasra-dala-kamala-karṇikā-madhya-niviṣṭa-guru-caraṇa-yugala-vigalad-amṛta-rasa-visara-pariplutâkhilâṅgo hṛdaya-kamala-madhye jvalantam udyad-aruṇa-koṭi-pāṭalam aśeṣa-doṣa-nirveṣa-bhūtam anekapânanaṃ niyamita-pavana-manogatir dhyātvā tat-prabhā-paṭala-pāṭalīkṛta-tanuḥ bahir nirgatya mukta-mala-mūtro danta-dhāvana-snāna-vastra-paridhāna-sūryârghya-dānāni vidhāya udyad-āditya-vartine mahā-gaṇapataye "tat-puruṣāya vidmahe, vakra-tuṇḍāya dhīmahi || tan no dantī pracodayāt" ity arghyaṃ datvā nitya-kṛtyaṃ vidhāya catur-āvṛtti-tarpaṇaṃ kuryāt | [69]
āyur ārogyam aiśvaryaṃ balaṃ puṣṭir mahad-yaśaḥ |
children.translated_text: Long life, health, sovereignty, strength, nourishment, great fame,

children.text: kavitvaṃ bhukti-muktī ca catur-āvṛtti-tarpaṇāt || Parks_2.2 ||
children.translated_text: poetic skill, enjoyment, and liberation — these come from the fourfold <s>tarpaṇa</s>. [Parks 2.2]

Rising in the <s>brāhma muhūrta</s> (pre-dawn hour), at the <s>dvādaśānta</s> (the point twelve finger-breadths above the head), having meditated upon the pair of guru's feet placed in the center of the pericarp of the thousand-petaled lotus, with one's entire body flooded by the stream of flowing nectar dripping from them, having meditated in the center of the heart-lotus upon a blazing, rosy-hued [deity], red like ten million rising suns, the destroyer of all faults, with many faces, with breath and mind controlled, one becomes rosy-bodied through that mass of radiance. Going outside, having relieved oneself and cleaned the teeth, performed bathing, put on garments, and offered <s>arghya</s> (water-offering) to the sun, one should give <s>arghya</s> to the great <s>Gaṇapati</s> who faces the rising sun, with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>: 'We know that <s>Puruṣa</s>, we meditate upon the curved-trunked one; may <s>Dantī</s> (the tusked one) impel us.' Having performed the daily rites, one should perform the fourfold <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation).

children.text: prathamaṃ dvādaśa-vāraṃ mūla-mantreṇa tarpayitvā mantrâṣṭāviṃśati-varṇān svāhā-'ntān ekaikaṃ catur-vāraṃ mūlaṃ ca catur-vāraṃ tarpayitvā punaḥ śrī-śrīpati-girijā-girijāpati-rati-ratipati-mahī-mahīpati-mahālakṣmī-mahālakṣmīpati-ṛddhy-āmoda-samṛddhi-pramoda-kānti-sumukha-madanāvatī-durmukha-madadravā-'vighnadrāviṇī-vighnakartṛ-vasudhārā-śaṅkhanidhi-vasumatī-padmanidhi-trayodaśa-mithuneṣv ekaikāṃ devatāṃ catur-vāraṃ mūlaṃ catur-vāraṃ ca tarpayet, evaṃ catuścatvāriṃśad-adhika-catuśśata-tarpaṇāni bhavanti || Parks_2.3 ||
children.translated_text: First, having offered <s>tarpaṇa</s> twelve times with the <s>mūlamantra</s> (root <s>mantra</s>), one should offer <s>tarpaṇa</s> for each of the twenty-eight syllables of the <s>mantra</s> ending with <s>svāhā</s>, four times each, and the root <s>mantra</s> four times. Then, for the thirteen divine couples — <s>Śrī</s> and <s>Śrīpati</s>, <s>Girijā</s> and <s>Girijāpati</s>, <s>Rati</s> and <s>Ratipati</s>, <s>Mahī</s> and <s>Mahīpati</s>, <s>Mahālakṣmī</s> and <s>Mahālakṣmīpati</s>, <s>Ṛddhi</s>-<s>Āmoda</s>, <s>Samṛddhi</s>-<s>Pramoda</s>, <s>Kānti</s>-<s>Sumukha</s>, <s>Madanāvatī</s>-<s>Durmukha</s>, <s>Madadravā</s>-<s>Avighna</s>, <s>Drāviṇī</s>-<s>Vighnakartṛ</s>, <s>Vasudhārā</s>-<s>Śaṅkhanidhi</s>, <s>Vasumatī</s>-<s>Padmanidhi</s> — one should offer <s>tarpaṇa</s> four times to each deity and the root <s>mantra</s> four times. Thus there are four hundred and forty-four <s>tarpaṇas</s> in total. [Parks 2.3]

children.text: atha yāga-vidhiḥ - gṛham āgatya sthaṇḍilam upalipya dvāra-deśa ubhaya-pārśvayor bhadra-kālyai bhairavāya - dvārordhve lambodarāya namaḥ iti antaḥpraviśya āsana-mantreṇa āsane sthitvā prāṇān āyamya ṣaḍ-aṅgāni vinyasya mūlena vyāpakaṃ kṛtvā svâtmani devaṃ siddhalakṣmī-samāśliṣṭa-pārśvam ardhendu-śekharam ārakta-varṇaṃ mātuluṅga-gadā-puṇḍrekṣu-kārmuka-śūla-sudarśana-śaṅkha-pāśotpala-dhānya-mañjarī-nija-dantâñcala-ratna-kalaśa-pariṣkṛta-pāṇy-ekādaśakaṃ prabhinna-kaṭam ānanda-pūrṇam aśeṣa-vighna-dhvaṃsa-nighnaṃ vighneśvaraṃ dhyātvā || Parks_2.4 ||
children.translated_text: Now the procedure for the <s>yāga</s> (worship): Having entered the house and smeared the altar (<s>sthaṇḍila</s>), at the doorway on both sides [offering] to <s>Bhadrakālī</s> and <s>Bhairava</s>, above the door [saluting] <s>Lambodara</s> (the pot-bellied one) with 'namaḥ,' and entering within, having sat on the seat with the seat-<s>mantra</s>, having regulated the breath (<s>prāṇāyāma</s>), having placed the six limbs (<s>ṣaḍaṅganyāsa</s>), having performed the pervasion (<s>vyāpaka</s>) with the root <s>mantra</s>, one should meditate upon the deity within oneself — <s>Vighneśvara</s> (Lord of Obstacles), embraced on either side by <s>Siddhalakṣmī</s>, with a crescent moon on his head, of reddish color, with hands adorned with a citron, mace, sugarcane bow, trident, <s>Sudarśana</s> (discus), conch, noose, lotus, grain-spike, his own tusk, and a jeweled vessel — eleven-handed, with a cleft forehead, filled with bliss, the destroyer of all obstacles. [Parks 2.4]

children.text: purato mūla-saptâbhimantritena gandhâkṣata-puṣpa-pūjitena śuddhena vāriṇā tri-koṇa-ṣaṭ-koṇa-vṛtta-catur-aśrāṇi vidhāya tasmin puṣpāṇi vikīrya vahnîśâsura-vāyuṣu madhye dikṣu ca ṣaḍ-aṅgāni vinyasya agni-maṇḍalāya daśa-kalā-''tmane arghya-pātrâdhārāya namaḥ sūrya-maṇḍalāya dvādaśa-kalā-''tmane arghya-pātrāya namaḥ soma-maṇḍalāya ṣoḍaśa-kalā-''tmane arghyâmṛtāya namaḥ iti śuddha-jalam āpūrya astreṇa saṃrakṣya kavacenâvakuṇṭhya dhenu-yoni-mudrāṃ pradarśayet || Parks_2.5 ||
children.translated_text: Before [the practitioner], having made triangles, hexagons, circles, and squares with pure water that has been consecrated seven times with the <s>mūla</s> (root mantra) and offered with sandalwood paste, unbroken rice, and flowers; having scattered flowers upon it; having placed the <s>ṣaḍaṅga</s> (six limbs of the mantra) at the positions of <s>Vahni</s> (Fire), <s>Īśa</s>, <s>Asura</s>, and <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind) in the middle and in the directions — 'Homage to the <s>agni-maṇḍala</s> (fire circle), whose essence is ten <s>kalās</s>, the support of the <s>arghya</s> (offering) vessel; homage to the <s>sūrya-maṇḍala</s> (sun circle), whose essence is twelve <s>kalās</s>, the <s>arghya</s> vessel; homage to the <s>soma-maṇḍala</s> (moon circle), whose essence is sixteen <s>kalās</s>, the <s>arghya</s> nectar' — thus filling with pure water, protecting with the <s>astra</s> (weapon mantra), covering with the <s>kavaca</s> (armor mantra), one should display the <s>dhenu-yoni-mudrā</s>.

children.text: sapta-vāram abhimantrya taj-jala-vipruḍbhir ātmānaṃ pūjopakaraṇāni ca saṃprokṣya taj-jalena pūrvoktaṃ maṇḍalaṃ parikalpya tadvad ādimaṃ saṃyojya tatro- [79] pādimaṃ madhyamaṃ ca nikṣipya vahny-arkendu-kalāḥ abhyarcya vakra-tuṇḍa-gāyatryā gaṇānāṃ tvety anayā ṛcā câbhimantrya astrâdi-rakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā tad-bindubhis triśaḥ śirasi guru-pādukām ārādhayet || Parks_2.6 ||
children.translated_text: Having consecrated seven times, sprinkling oneself and the worship implements with drops of that water, constructing the previously described <s>maṇḍala</s> with that water, joining the first element as before, placing the last and middle elements upon it, worshipping the <s>kalās</s> of fire, sun, and moon, consecrating with the <s>Vakratuṇḍa Gāyatrī</s> beginning with '<s>gaṇānāṃ tvā</s>' and with this <s>ṛc</s> (Vedic verse), performing protection with <s>astra</s> etc., with its drops three times upon the head, one should worship the <s>guru-pādukā</s> (the sandals of the teacher).

children.text: purato rakta-candana-nirmite pīṭhe mahā-gaṇapati-pratimāyāṃ vā catur-asrâṣṭa-dala-ṣaṭ-koṇa-tri-koṇa-maye cakre vā tīvrāyai jvālinyai nandāyai bhogadāyai kāmarūpiṇyai ugrāyai tejovatyai satyāyai vighnanāśinyai ṛṃ dharmāya ṝṃ jñānāya ḷṃ vairāgyāya ḹṃ aiśvaryāya ṛṃ adharmāya ṝṃ ajñānāya ḷṃ avairāgyāya ḹṃ anaiśvaryāya nama iti pīṭha-śaktīr dharmâdy-aṣṭakaṃ câbhyarcya mūlam uccārya mahā-gaṇapatim āvāhayāmîty āvāhya pañcadhopacarya daśadhā saṃtarpya mūlena mithunâṅga-brāhmy-ādîndrâdi-rūpa-pañcâvaraṇa-pūjāṃ kuryāt || Parks_2.7 ||
children.translated_text: Before [the practitioner], on a seat made of red sandalwood, or upon an image of <s>Mahāgaṇapati</s>, or upon a <s>cakra</s> consisting of a square, eight petals, hexagon, and triangle — [worshipping] <s>Tīvrā</s>, <s>Jvālinī</s>, <s>Nandā</s>, <s>Bhogadā</s>, <s>Kāmarūpiṇī</s>, <s>Ugrā</s>, <s>Tejovatī</s>, <s>Satyā</s>, <s>Vighnanāśinī</s>; 'ṛṃ to <s>Dharma</s>, ṝṃ to <s>Jñāna</s>, ḷṃ to <s>Vairāgya</s>, ḹṃ to <s>Aiśvarya</s>, ṛṃ to <s>Adharma</s>, ṝṃ to <s>Ajñāna</s>, ḷṃ to <s>Avairāgya</s>, ḹṃ to <s>Anaiśvarya</s>, namaḥ' — thus worshipping the <s>pīṭha-śaktis</s> (seat powers) and the eightfold group beginning with <s>Dharma</s>, uttering the <s>mūla</s> (root mantra), invoking <s>Mahāgaṇapati</s> with 'I invoke <s>Mahāgaṇapati</s>,' offering the fivefold worship, satisfying with tenfold offerings, one should perform the <s>pañcāvaraṇa-pūjā</s> (five-covering worship) in the form of the consort-limbs and <s>Brāhmī</s> etc. and <s>Indra</s> etc. with the <s>mūla</s> mantra.

children.text: tri-koṇe devaḥ tasya ṣaḍ-asrasyântarāle śrī-śrīpaty-ādi-catur-mithunāni aṅgāni ca ṛddhy-āmodâdi-ṣaṇ-mithunāni ṣaḍ-asre mithuna-dvayaṃ ṣaḍ-asrobhaya-pārśvayos tat-sandhiṣv aṅgāni brāhmy-ādyā aṣṭa-dale catur-asrâṣṭa-dikṣv indrâdyāḥ pūjyāḥ sarvatra devatā-nāmasu śrī-pūrvaṃ pādukām uccārya pūjayāmîty aṣṭâkṣarīṃ yojayet || Parks_2.8 ||
children.translated_text: In the triangle is the deity; in the interstice of his hexagon are the four couples beginning with <s>Śrī</s> and <s>Śrīpati</s>, and the <s>aṅgas</s> (limbs), and the six couples beginning with <s>Ṛddhi</s> and <s>Āmoda</s> in the hexagon, two couples on the hexagon, on both sides of the hexagon at its junctions are the <s>aṅgas</s>; <s>Brāhmī</s> and others on the eight petals; <s>Indra</s> and others in the eight directions of the square are to be worshipped. In all deity names, one should join the <s>aṣṭākṣarī</s> (eight-syllable mantra) prefixed with 'Śrī,' uttering the <s>pādukā</s> and 'I worship.'

children.text: evaṃ pañcâvaraṇīm iṣṭvā punar devaṃ gaṇanāthaṃ daśadhopatarpya ṣoḍaśopacārair upacarya praṇava-māyā-'nte sarva-vighna-kṛdbhyaḥ sarva-bhūtebhyo huṃ svāhā - iti triḥ paṭhitvā baliṃ datvā gaṇapati-buddhyaikaṃ baṭukaṃ siddhalakṣmī-buddhyaikāṃ śaktiṃ câhūya gandha-puṣpâkṣatair abhyarcyâdimopādima-madhyamān datvā mama nirvighnaṃ mantra-siddhir bhūyād ity anugrahaṃ kārayitvā namaskṛtya yathā-śakti japet || Parks_2.9 ||
children.translated_text: Having thus worshipped the five coverings, again satisfying Lord <s>Gaṇanātha</s> with tenfold offerings and worshipping with the sixteen <s>upacāras</s> (modes of worship), reciting three times 'to all obstacle-makers, to all beings, huṃ svāhā' after <s>praṇava</s> and <s>māyā</s>, giving the <s>bali</s> (offering), inviting one <s>baṭuka</s> with the understanding of <s>Gaṇapati</s> and one <s>śakti</s> with the understanding of <s>Siddhalakṣmī</s>, worshipping with sandalwood paste, flowers, and unbroken rice, offering the first, last, and middle portions, having them bestow the blessing 'may <s>mantra-siddhi</s> (perfection of mantra) come to me without obstacles,' bowing, one should recite the mantra according to one's ability.

children.text: yady agni-kārya-saṃpattiḥ baleḥ pūrvaṃ vidhi-vat saṃskṛte 'gnau svāhā-'ntaiḥ śrī-śrīpaty-ādi-vighnakartṛ-paryantaiḥ mantrair hutvā punar āgatya devaṃ tri-vāraṃ saṃtarpya yogyais saha ma-pañcakam urarī-kṛtya mahā-gaṇapatim ātmany udvāsya siddha-saṅkalpaḥ sukhī viharet iti śivam || Parks_2.10 ||
children.translated_text: If there is the means for a fire ceremony, before the <s>bali</s> offering, having offered oblations into the duly consecrated fire with mantras ending in svāhā from those of <s>Śrī</s>-<s>Śrīpati</s> etc. up to <s>Vighnakartṛ</s> (the obstacle-maker), again returning and satisfying the deity three times, accepting the <s>ma-pañcaka</s> (five substances beginning with 'ma') with the worthy ones, dissolving <s>Mahāgaṇapati</s> into oneself, one of fulfilled intention should dwell happily. Thus, auspiciousness.

children.text: 3. Khaṇḍa: Śrī-krama
children.translated_text: Chapter 3: <s>Śrī-krama</s> (The Procedure of Śrī)

children.text: evaṃ gaṇapatim iṣṭvā vidhūta-samasta-vighna-vyatikaraḥ śakti-cakraika-nāyikāyāḥ śrī-lalitāyāḥ kramam ārabheta || Parks_3.1 ||
children.translated_text: Having thus worshipped <s>Gaṇapati</s>, freed from the entanglement of all obstacles, one should begin the procedure of <s>Śrī Lalitā</s>, the sole heroine of the circle of <s>śaktis</s>.

children.text: brāhme muhūrte brāhmaṇo mukta-svāpaḥ pāpa-vilāpāya parama-śiva-rūpaṃ gurum abhimṛśya || Parks_3.2 ||
children.translated_text: At the <s>brahma-muhūrta</s> (the auspicious pre-dawn hour), a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, having risen from sleep, should contemplate the <s>guru</s> in the form of <s>Paramaśiva</s> for the destruction of sins.

children.text: mūlâdi-vidhi-bila-paryantaṃ taḍit-koṭi-kaḍārāṃ taruṇa-divākara-piñjarāṃ jvalantīṃ mūla-saṃvidaṃ dhyātvā tad-raśmi-nihata-kaśmala-jālaḥ kâdiṃ hâdiṃ vā mūla-vidyāṃ manasā daśavāram āvartya || Parks_3.3 ||
children.translated_text: Meditating upon the <s>mūla-saṃvid</s> (root consciousness), blazing, tawny like the rising sun, with the brilliance of ten million lightning bolts, from the root according to the prescribed procedure to the end of the <s>bila</s> (opening); with the net of impurities destroyed by her rays, mentally repeating the <s>mūla-vidyā</s> (root knowledge mantra) — either the <s>kādi</s> or the <s>hādi</s> — ten times.

children.text: snāna-karmaṇi prāpte mūlena datvā triḥ salilâñjalīn tris tad-abhimantritāḥ pītvā 'pas tris santarpya triḥ prokṣyâtmānaṃ paridhāya vāsasī hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ saḥ ity uktvā mārtâṇḍa-bhairavāya prakāśa-śakti-sahitāya svāheti tris savitre dattârghyaḥ || Parks_3.4 ||
children.translated_text: When the time for bathing has arrived, offering three handfuls of water with the <s>mūla</s> mantra, drinking water consecrated by it three times, satisfying [the deities] three times, sprinkling oneself three times, putting on garments, saying 'hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ saḥ,' one should offer <s>arghya</s> three times to <s>Savitṛ</s> with 'to <s>Mārtāṇḍa Bhairava</s> together with <s>Prakāśa Śakti</s>, svāhā.'

children.text: tan-maṇḍala-madhye nava-yoni-cakram anucintya vācam uccārya tripura-sundari vidmahe kāmam uccārya pīṭha-kāmini dhīmahi - śaktim uccārya, tan naḥ klinnā pracodayād iti - trir maheśyai dattârghyaḥ śatam aṣṭottaram āmṛśya manuṃ maunam ālambya || Parks_3.5 ||
children.translated_text: Contemplating the <s>nava-yoni-cakra</s> (nine-triangle diagram) in the middle of that <s>maṇḍala</s>, uttering the <s>vāc</s> (speech) mantra, 'We know <s>Tripurasundarī</s>,' uttering <s>Kāma</s>, 'O <s>Pīṭha-Kāminī</s>, we meditate,' uttering the <s>Śakti</s>, 'May <s>Klinnā</s> inspire us' — thus offering <s>arghya</s> three times to <s>Maheśī</s>, touching the <s>manu</s> (mantra) one hundred and eight times, observing silence.

children.text: yāga-mandiraṃ gatvā kḷptâkalpas saṅkalpâkalpo vā pīṭha-manunā āsane samupaviṣṭaḥ || Parks_3.6 ||
children.translated_text: Going to the worship hall, either fully adorned or without adornment, one should be seated on a seat with the <s>pīṭha-manu</s> (seat mantra).

children.text: tritārīm uccārya rakta-dvādaśa-śakti-yuktāya dīpa-nāthāya nama iti bhūmau muñcet puṣpâñjalim || Parks_3.7 ||
children.translated_text: Uttering the <s>tritārī</s>, one should release the <s>puṣpāñjali</s> (handful of flowers) onto the ground saying 'Homage to the Lord of Lights endowed with the twelve red <s>śaktis</s>.'

children.text: sarveṣāṃ mantrāṇām ādau tritārī-saṃyogaḥ | tritārī vāṅ-māyā-kamalāḥ || Parks_3.8 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>tritārī</s> is to be joined at the beginning of all mantras. The <s>tritārī</s> consists of <s>Vāk</s> (Speech), <s>Māyā</s>, and <s>Kamalā</s> (Lotus).

children.text: purataḥ pañca-śakti-catuḥ-śrīkaṇṭha-melana-rūpaṃ bhū-sadana-traya-vali-traya-bhūpa-patra-dik-patra-bhuvanâra-druhiṇâra-vidhi-koṇa-dik-koṇa-trikoṇa-bindu-cakra-mayaṃ mahā-cakra-rājaṃ sindūra-kuṅkuma-likhitaṃ cāmīkara-kala-dhauta-pañca-loha-ratna-sphaṭikâdy-utkīrṇaṃ vā niveśya || Parks_3.9 ||
children.translated_text: Before [the practitioner], one should place the great <s>Śrīcakra-rāja</s> — consisting of the form of the union of the five <s>śaktis</s> and four <s>Śrīkaṇṭhas</s>, comprising the <s>bhūpura</s>-triad, <s>vali</s>-triad, <s>bhūpa-patra</s>, <s>dik-patra</s>, <s>bhuvana</s>-petals, <s>Druhiṇa</s>-petals, <s>vidhi</s>-angles, <s>dik</s>-angles, triangle, and <s>bindu-cakra</s> — drawn with vermilion and saffron, or engraved on gold, silver, five metals, gems, crystal, and the like.

children.text: tatra mahā-cakre amṛtâmbhonidhaye ratna-dvīpāya nānā-vṛkṣa-mahodyānāya kalpa-vṛkṣa-vāṭikāyai santāna-vāṭikāyai hari-candana-vāṭikāyai mandāra-vāṭikāyai pārijāta-vāṭikāyai kadamba-vāṭikāyai puṣpa-rāga-ratna-prākārāya padma-rāga-ratna-prākārāya go-medha-ratna-prākārāya vajra-ratna-prākārāya vaiḍūrya-ratna-prākārāya indra-nīla-ratna-prākārāya muktā-ratna-prākārāya marakata-ratna-prākārāya vidruma-ratna-prākārāya māṇikya-maṇḍapāya sahasra-stambha-maṇḍapāya amṛta-vāpikāyai ānanda-vāpikāyai vimarśa-vāpikāyai bālâtapodgārāya candrikodgārāya mahā-śṛṅgāra-parighāyai mahā-padmâṭavyai cintā-maṇi-gṛha-rājāya pūrvâmnāya-maya-pūrva-dvārāya dakṣiṇâmnāya-maya-dakṣiṇa-dvārāya paścimâmnāya-maya-paścima-dvārāyottarâmnāya-mayottara-dvārāya ratna-pradīpa-valayāya maṇi-maya-mahā-siṃhâsanāya brahma-mayaika-mañca-pādāya viṣṇu-mayaika-mañca-pādāya rudra-mayaika-mañca-pādāya īśvara-mayaika-mañca-pādāya sadāśiva-mayaika-mañca-phalakāya haṃsa-tūla-talpāya haṃsa-tūla-mahopadhānāya kausumbhâstaraṇāya mahā-vitānakāya mahā-javanikāyai namaḥ - iti catuścatvāriṃśan-mantrais tat-tad akhilaṃ bhāvayitvā arcayitvā || Parks_3.10 ||
children.translated_text: There in the great <s>cakra</s> — to the ocean of nectar, to the jeweled island, to the great garden of various trees, to the grove of wish-fulfilling trees, to the grove of <s>Santāna</s> trees, to the grove of <s>Haricandana</s> (sandalwood) trees, to the grove of <s>Mandāra</s> trees, to the grove of <s>Pārijāta</s> trees, to the grove of <s>Kadamba</s> trees, to the rampart of <s>Puṣparāga</s> gems, to the rampart of <s>Padmarāga</s> gems, to the rampart of <s>Gomedha</s> gems, to the rampart of <s>Vajra</s> (diamond) gems, to the rampart of <s>Vaiḍūrya</s> (cat's-eye) gems, to the rampart of <s>Indranīla</s> (sapphire) gems, to the rampart of <s>Muktā</s> (pearl) gems, to the rampart of <s>Marakata</s> (emerald) gems, to the rampart of <s>Vidruma</s> (coral) gems, to the <s>Māṇikya</s> (ruby) pavilion, to the thousand-pillared pavilion, to the pool of nectar, to the pool of bliss, to the pool of reflection, to the radiance of the young sun, to the radiance of moonlight, to the great garden of love, to the great lotus forest, to the king of houses made of <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gems), to the eastern gate made of the eastern tradition, to the southern gate made of the southern tradition, to the western gate made of the western tradition, to the northern gate made of the northern tradition, to the ring of gem-lamps, to the great lion-throne made of gems, to one leg of the couch made of <s>Brahmā</s>, to one leg of the couch made of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, to one leg of the couch made of <s>Rudra</s>, to one leg of the couch made of <s>Īśvara</s>, to the plank of the couch made of <s>Sadāśiva</s>, to the mattress of swan-down, to the great pillow of swan-down, to the bedspread of <s>Kausumbha</s> (safflower silk), to the great canopy, to the great curtain, namaḥ — thus contemplating and worshipping all of these with forty-four mantras.

children.text: gandha-puṣpâkṣatâdīṃś ca dakṣiṇa-bhāge dīpān abhito dattvā mūlena cakram abhyarcya mūla-tri-khaṇḍaiḥ prathama-try-asre || Parks_3.11 ||
children.translated_text: Having placed sandalwood paste, flowers, unbroken rice, etc. and lamps on both sides to the right, worshipping the <s>cakra</s> with the <s>mūla</s> mantra, [one should worship] the first triad of triangles with the three sections of the <s>mūla</s> mantra.

children.text: vāyv-agni-salila-varṇa-yuk-prāṇâyāmaiḥ śoṣaṇaṃ saṃdahanam āplāvanaṃ ca vidhāya || Parks_3.12 ||
children.translated_text: Performing desiccation, burning, and flooding with <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> (breath controls) of the colors of wind, fire, and water.

children.text: triḥ prāṇān āyamya || Parks_3.13 ||
children.translated_text: Restraining the breath three times.

children.text: apasarpantu te bhūtā ye bhūtā bhuvi saṃsthitāḥ |
children.translated_text: May those beings who are beings dwelling on earth depart;

children.text: ye bhūtā vighna-kartāras te naśyantu śivâjñayā |
children.translated_text: May those beings who are obstacle-makers be destroyed by the command of <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: iti vāma-pāda-pārṣṇi-ghāta-karâsphoṭa-samudañcita-vaktras tāla-trayaṃ datvā devy-aham-bhāva-yuktaḥ sva-śarīre vajra-kavaca-nyāsa-jālaṃ vidadhīta || Parks_3.14 ||
children.translated_text: Thus, with face raised by striking the left heel and clapping the hands, giving three claps, endowed with the sense of identity with the <s>Devī</s> (Goddess), one should perform the network of <s>vajra-kavaca-nyāsa</s> (diamond-armor placement) on one's own body.

children.text: bindu-yuk-śrīkaṇṭhânanta-tārtīyaiḥ madhyamâdi-tala-paryantaṃ kṛta-kara-śuddhiḥ || Parks_3.15 ||
children.translated_text: Having purified the hands from the middle finger to the end of the palm with [mantras of] <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>, <s>Ananta</s>, and the third, joined with <s>bindu</s>.

children.text: kumārīm uccārya mahā-tripurasundarī-padam ātmānaṃ rakṣa rakṣeti hṛdaye añjaliṃ dattvā || Parks_3.16 ||
children.translated_text: Uttering '<s>Kumārī</s>,' placing the <s>añjali</s> (joined palms) on the heart saying 'O <s>Mahā-Tripurasundarī</s>, protect, protect me.'

children.text: māyā-kāma-śaktīr uccārya devy-ātmâsanāya namaḥ - iti svasyâsanaṃ dattvā || Parks_3.17 ||
children.translated_text: Uttering the <s>Māyā</s>-<s>Kāma</s>-<s>Śaktis</s>, giving one's own seat with 'Homage to the seat of the <s>Devī-Ātman</s> (Goddess-Self).'

children.text: śiva-yug-bālām uccārya śrī-cakrâsanāya namaḥ - śiva-bhṛgu-yug-bālām uccārya sarva-mantrâsanāya - namo bhuvanā-madanau blem uccārya sādhya-siddhâsanāya namaḥ - iti cakra-mantra-devatā-''sanaṃ tribhir mantraiś cakre kṛtvā || Parks_3.18 ||
children.translated_text: Having uttered the <s>Śiva</s>-joined <s>Bālā</s> [mantra], 'to the seat of <s>Śrī Cakra</s>, salutation' — having uttered the <s>Śiva</s>-<s>Bhṛgu</s>-joined <s>Bālā</s> [mantra], 'to the seat of all <s>mantras</s>, salutation' — having uttered <s>Bhuvanā</s> and <s>Madana</s> with blēṃ, 'to the seat of <s>Sādhya-siddha</s> (that which is to be accomplished and perfected), salutation' — thus the <s>āsana</s> (seat) of the <s>cakra</s>, <s>mantra</s>, and <s>devatā</s> (deity) is established in the <s>cakra</s> with three <s>mantras</s>. || Parks_3.18 ||

children.text: bālā-dvir-āvṛttyā tri-dvy-eka-daśa-tri-dvi-saṅkhyā-'ṅguli-vinyāsaiḥ kḷpta-ṣaḍ-aṅgaḥ || Parks_3.19 ||
children.translated_text: With two repetitions of <s>Bālā</s> [mantra], the <s>ṣaḍaṅga</s> (six limbs) is accomplished through finger-placements in the sequence of three, two, one, ten, three, and two. || Parks_3.19 ||

children.text: sa-bindūn aco blūm uccārya vaśinī-vāg-devatāyai namaḥ - iti śirasi | sarvatra vargāṇāṃ bindu-yogaḥ | ka-vargaṃ ka-la-hrīṃ ca nigadya kāmeśvarī-vāg-devatāyai namaḥ - iti lalāṭe | cuṃ gaditvā nvlīṃ modinī-vāg-devatāyai namaḥ - iti bhrū-madhye | ṭuṃ bhaṇitvā ylūṃ vimalā-vāg-devatāyai namaḥ - iti kaṇṭhe | tuṃ ca procya jmrīṃ aruṇā-vāg-devatāyai namaḥ - iti hṛdi | puṃ ca hslvyūṃ uccārya jayinī-vāg-devatāyai namaḥ - iti nābhau | yâdi-catuṣkaṃ jhmryūṃ uccārya sarveśvarī-vāg-devatāyai namaḥ - iti liṅge | śâdi-ṣaṭkaṃ kṣmrīṃ ākhyāya kaulinī-vāg-devatāyai namaḥ - iti mūle || Parks_3.20 ||
children.translated_text: Having uttered the vowels with <s>bindu</s> (nasal dot) as blūṃ, 'to <s>Vaśinī</s>, the deity of speech, salutation' — thus on the head. Everywhere the <s>bindu</s> is joined to the consonant groups. Having pronounced the ka-group and ka-la-hrīṃ, 'to <s>Kāmeśvarī</s>, the deity of speech, salutation' — thus on the forehead. Having said cuṃ and nvlīṃ, 'to <s>Modinī</s>, the deity of speech, salutation' — thus between the eyebrows. Having pronounced ṭuṃ and ylūṃ, 'to <s>Vimalā</s>, the deity of speech, salutation' — thus on the throat. Having uttered tuṃ and jmrīṃ, 'to <s>Aruṇā</s>, the deity of speech, salutation' — thus on the heart. Having uttered puṃ and hslvyūṃ, 'to <s>Jayinī</s>, the deity of speech, salutation' — thus on the navel. Having uttered the four beginning with ya and jhmryūṃ, 'to <s>Sarveśvarī</s>, the deity of speech, salutation' — thus on the <s>liṅga</s> (generative organ). Having pronounced the six beginning with śa and kṣmrīṃ, 'to <s>Kaulinī</s>, the deity of speech, salutation' — thus at the base. || Parks_3.20 ||

children.text: mūla-vidyā-pañcadaśa-varṇān mūrdhni mūle hṛdi cakṣus-tritaye śruti-dvaya-mukha-bhuja-yugala-pṛṣṭha-jānu-yugala-nābhiṣu vinyasya ṣoḍhā cakre nyasyânyasya vā || Parks_3.21 ||
children.translated_text: Having placed the fifteen syllables of the <s>mūla-vidyā</s> (root mantra) on the crown, the base, the heart, the three eyes, the two ears, the mouth, the two arms, the back, the two knees, and the navel, one should perform <s>nyāsa</s> (ritual placement) in the <s>cakra</s> in six ways, or alternatively [place them otherwise]. || Parks_3.21 ||

children.text: śuddhâmbhasā vāma-bhāge tri-koṇa-ṣaṭ-koṇa-vṛtta-catur-aśra-maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā puṣpair abhyarcya sâdhāraṃ śaṅkhaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya śuddha-jalam āpūrya ādima-binduṃ dattvā ṣaḍ-aṅgenâbhyarcya vidyayā abhimantrya taj-jala-vipruḍbhiḥ ātmānaṃ pūjopakaraṇāni ca saṃprokṣya || Parks_3.22 ||
children.translated_text: Having made a <s>maṇḍala</s> (sacred diagram) of triangle, hexagon, circle, and square on the left side with pure water, having worshipped with flowers, having established a conch shell with its base, having filled it with pure water, having given the first <s>bindu</s>, having worshipped with the <s>ṣaḍaṅga</s> (six limbs), having consecrated it with the <s>vidyā</s> (mantra), one should sprinkle oneself and the worship implements with drops of that water. || Parks_3.22 ||

children.text: taj-jalena tri-koṇa-ṣaṭ-koṇa-vṛtta-catur-asra-maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā madhyaṃ vidyayā vidyā-khaṇḍais tri-koṇaṃ bījâvṛttyā ṣaḍ-aśraṃ saṃpūjya vācam uccārya agni-maṇḍa- [107] lāya daśa-kalā-''tmane arghya-pātrâdhārāya namaḥ - iti pratiṣṭhāpya ādhāraṃ prapūjya pāvakīḥ kalāḥ || Parks_3.23 ||
children.translated_text: Having made a <s>maṇḍala</s> (sacred diagram) of triangle, hexagon, circle, and square with that water, having worshipped the center with the <s>vidyā</s> (mantra), the triangle with the divisions of the <s>vidyā</s>, the hexagon with repetition of the <s>bīja</s> (seed syllable), and having uttered the invocation, 'to the <s>Agni-maṇḍala</s> (fire circle), whose nature is the ten <s>kalās</s> (phases), to the support of the <s>arghya</s> (offering) vessel, salutation' — thus having established [it], one should worship the support and the <s>kalās</s> of fire. || Parks_3.23 ||

children.text: madanād upari sūrya-maṇḍalāya dvādaśa-kalā-''tmane arghya-pātrāya namaḥ iti saṃvidhāya pātraṃ saṃspṛśya kalāḥ saurīḥ sauḥ soma-maṇḍalāya ṣoḍaśa-kalā-''tmane arghyâmṛtāya namaḥ - iti pūrayitvā ādimaṃ dattvopādima-madhyamau pūjayitvā vidhoḥ kalā-ṣoḍaśakam || Parks_3.24 ||
children.translated_text: Above <s>Madana</s>, having arranged [saying] 'to the <s>Sūrya-maṇḍala</s> (solar circle), whose nature is the twelve <s>kalās</s> (phases), to the <s>arghya</s> (offering) vessel, salutation,' having touched the vessel, [one should worship] the solar <s>kalās</s>. [Then saying] sauḥ, 'to the <s>Soma-maṇḍala</s> (lunar circle), whose nature is the sixteen <s>kalās</s> (phases), to the nectar of the <s>arghya</s> (offering), salutation' — thus having filled [it], having given the first [offering] and having worshipped the second and middle ones, [one should worship] the sixteen <s>kalās</s> of the moon. || Parks_3.24 ||

children.text: tatra vilikhya try-asram a-ka-thâdi-maya-rekhaṃ ha-la-kṣa-yugânta-sthita-haṃsa-bhāsvaraṃ vāk-kāma-śakti-yukta-koṇaṃ haṃsenârādhya bahir vṛtta-ṣaṭ-koṇaṃ kṛtvā ṣaḍ-asraṃ ṣaḍ-aṅgena puro-bhāgâdy abhyarcya mūlena saptadhā abhimantrya datta-gandhâkṣata-puṣpa-dhūpa-dīpaḥ tad-vipruḍbhiḥ prokṣita-pūjā-dravyaḥ sarvaṃ vidyāmayaṃ kṛtvā tat spṛṣṭvā caturnavati-mantrān japet || Parks_3.25 ||
children.translated_text: There, having drawn a triangle with lines formed of a-ka-tha and other [syllables], radiant with <s>Haṃsa</s> stationed at the end of ha-la-kṣa pair, with corners endowed with <s>Vāk</s> (speech), <s>Kāma</s> (desire), and <s>Śakti</s> (power), having worshipped with <s>Haṃsa</s>, having made an outer circle and hexagon, having worshipped the hexagon with the <s>ṣaḍaṅga</s> (six limbs) beginning from the front, having consecrated seven times with the <s>mūla</s> (root mantra), having offered incense, lamps, sandal paste, unbroken rice, and flowers, having sprinkled the worship materials with drops of that [water], having made everything pervaded by the <s>vidyā</s> (mantra), having touched that, one should recite the ninety-four <s>mantras</s>. || Parks_3.25 ||

children.text: tritārī-namas-saṃpuṭitāḥ tejas-tritaya-kalā aṣṭatriṃśat |
children.translated_text: The <s>kalās</s> (phases) of the three luminaries, enclosed by the triple tārī and namaḥ, are thirty-eight.

children.text: sṛṣṭi-ṛddhi-smṛti-medhā-kānti-lakṣmī-dyuti-sthirā-sthiti-siddhayo brahma-kalā daśa | jarā pālinī śāntir īśvarī rati-kāmike varadâhlādinī prītir dīrghā viṣṇu-kalā daśa | tīkṣṇā raudrī bhayā nidrā tandrī kṣudhā krodhinī kriyodgārī-mṛtyavo rudra-kalā daśa | pītā śvetā-'ruṇā-'sitāś catasra īśvara-kalāḥ | nivṛtti-pratiṣṭhā-vidyā-śāntîndhikā-dīpikā-recikā-mocikā-parā-sūkṣmā-sūkṣmâmṛtā-jñānā-jñānâmṛtā-pyāyinī-vyāpinī-vyomarūpāḥ ṣoḍaśa sadāśiva-kalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Creation, prosperity, memory, intelligence, radiance, fortune, splendor, steadiness, stability, and perfection — these are the ten <s>kalās</s> of <s>Brahmā</s>. Old age, the protectress, peace, sovereignty, passion, desire, the boon-giver, the gladdener, affection, and endurance — these are the ten <s>kalās</s> of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. The sharp one, the fierce one, fear, sleep, sloth, hunger, the wrathful one, activity, expulsion, and death — these are the ten <s>kalās</s> of <s>Rudra</s>. The yellow, the white, the reddish, and the dark — these are the four <s>kalās</s> of <s>Īśvara</s>. <s>Nivṛtti</s> (cessation), <s>Pratiṣṭhā</s> (establishment), <s>Vidyā</s> (knowledge), <s>Śānti</s> (peace), <s>Indhikā</s> (the kindler), <s>Dīpikā</s> (the illuminator), <s>Recikā</s> (the emptier), <s>Mocikā</s> (the liberator), <s>Parā</s> (the supreme), <s>Sūkṣmā</s> (the subtle), <s>Sūkṣmāmṛtā</s> (the subtle nectar), <s>Jñānā</s> (knowledge), <s>Jñānāmṛtā</s> (the nectar of knowledge), <s>Āpyāyinī</s> (the nourisher), <s>Vyāpinī</s> (the pervader), and <s>Vyomarūpā</s> (sky-formed) — these are the sixteen <s>kalās</s> of <s>Sadāśiva</s>.

children.text: haṃsaś śuci-ṣad vasur antarikṣa-sad dhotā vvedi-ṣad atithir duroṇa-sat |
children.translated_text: The <s>Haṃsa</s> (swan), dwelling in brightness, the <s>Vasu</s> (good one), dwelling in the atmosphere, the <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoker), dwelling at the altar, the guest, dwelling in the house —

children.text: nṛ-ṣad vara-sad ṛta-sad vayoma-sad ab-jā go-jā ṛta-jā adri-jā ṛtaṃ bṛhat ||
children.translated_text: Dwelling among men, dwelling in the noble, dwelling in <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order), dwelling in the sky, born of water, born of cattle, born of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order), born of the mountain — [that] <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic truth) is vast.

children.text: pra tad-viṣṇuḥ stavate vīryeṇa mṛgo na bhīmaḥ ku-caro giri-ṣṭhāḥ |
children.translated_text: That <s>Viṣṇu</s> is praised for his valor, like a fearsome wild beast roaming the mountains, dwelling on the heights,

children.text: yasyoruṣu triṣu vikrameṣv adhikṣiyanti bhuvanāni vviśvā ||
children.translated_text: In whose three wide strides all the worlds abide.

children.text: tryambakaṃ yajāmahe su-gandhiṃ puṣṭi-vardhanam |
children.translated_text: We worship the three-eyed one, the fragrant one, the increaser of nourishment;

children.text: urvārukam iva bandhanān mṛtyor mukṣīya mâmṛtāt ||
children.translated_text: As a cucumber [is released] from its stem, may I be freed from death, not from immortality.

children.text: tad-viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ sadā paśyanti sūrayaḥ |
children.translated_text: The supreme abode of that <s>Viṣṇu</s> the wise ones always behold,

children.text: divîva cakṣur ātatam ||
children.translated_text: Like an eye spread across the sky.

children.text: tad-viprāso vipanyavo jāgṛ-vāṃsaḥ samindhate |
children.translated_text: That [abode] the inspired sages, ever wakeful, kindle with their hymns —

children.text: viṣṇor yat paramaṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: That supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: viṣṇur yoniṃ kalpayatu tvaṣṭā rūpāṇi piṃśatu |
children.translated_text: May <s>Viṣṇu</s> prepare the womb, may <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> fashion the forms,

children.text: āsiñcatu prajāpatir dhātā garbhaṃ dadhātu te ||
children.translated_text: May <s>Prajāpati</s> pour forth, may <s>Dhātṛ</s> place the embryo in you.

children.text: garbhaṃ dhehi sinīvāli garbhaṃ dhehi sarasvati |
children.translated_text: Place the embryo, O <s>Sinīvālī</s>; place the embryo, O <s>Sarasvatī</s>;

children.text: garbhaṃ te aśvinau devāv ādhattāṃ puṣkara-srajā ||
children.translated_text: May the two divine <s>Aśvins</s>, wreathed in lotuses, place the embryo in you.

children.text: ity ete pañca-mantrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus these are the five <s>mantras</s>.

children.text: mūla-vidyā câhatya caturnavati-mantrāḥ || Parks_3.26 ||
children.translated_text: Together with the <s>mūla-vidyā</s> (root mantra), [they total] ninety-four <s>mantras</s>. || Parks_3.26 ||

children.text: atha haike pañcabhir akhaṇḍâdyair abhimantraṇam āmananti || Parks_3.27 ||
children.translated_text: Now, some teach the consecration with five [mantras] beginning with <s>Akhaṇḍa</s> (the undivided). || Parks_3.27 ||

children.text: akhaṇḍaika-rasânanda-kare para-sudhā-''tmani |
children.translated_text: O you who create undivided, singular, essential bliss, who are of the nature of supreme nectar,

children.text: sva-cchanda-sphuraṇam atra nidhehy akula-nāyike ||
children.translated_text: Place spontaneous manifestation here, O leader of <s>Akula</s> (the transcendent).

children.text: akula-sthâmṛtâkāre śuddha-jñāna-kare pare |
children.translated_text: O you who are established in <s>Akula</s> (the transcendent), whose form is nectar, who bestow pure knowledge, O supreme one,

children.text: amṛtatvaṃ nidhehy asmin vastuni klinna-rūpiṇi ||
children.translated_text: Place immortality in this substance, O you whose form is moist [with grace].

children.text: tad-rūpiṇy aikarasyatvaṃ kṛtvā hy etat sva-rūpiṇi |
children.translated_text: O you who are of that form, having made oneness of essence with this, being of one's own true form,

children.text: bhūtvā parâmṛtâkārā mayi cit-sphuraṇaṃ kuru ||
children.translated_text: Having become of the nature of supreme nectar, cause the flash of consciousness to arise in me.

children.text: iti tisro 'nuṣṭubho vidyāḥ || Parks_3.28 ||
children.translated_text: Thus [there are] three <s>vidyās</s> (mantras) in <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> (meter). || Parks_3.28 ||

children.text: atho vācaṃ blūṃ jhraum iti jūṃ saḥ - iti coktvā amṛte amṛtodbhave amṛteśvari amṛta-varṣiṇi amṛtaṃ srāvaya srāvaya svāheti caturtho mantraḥ || Parks_3.29 ||
children.translated_text: Then having uttered the speech-syllable blūṃ jhraum and also jūṃ saḥ — [one recites]: '<s>Amṛtā</s> (O immortal one), <s>Amṛtodbhavā</s> (O you born of nectar), <s>Amṛteśvarī</s> (O sovereign of nectar), <s>Amṛtavarṣiṇī</s> (O you who shower nectar), cause the nectar to flow, cause it to flow, <s>svāhā</s>' — this is the fourth <s>mantra</s>. || Parks_3.29 ||

children.text: vāgbhavo vada vada tato vāg-vādini vāṅ-madana-klinne kledini kledaya mahā-kṣobhaṃ kuru-yugalaṃ mādanaṃ śaktir mokṣaṃ kuru kuru śabdo ha-sa-caturdaśa-pañcadaśa-piṇḍaḥ sa-ha-caturdaśa-ṣoḍaśa-piṇḍaś ceti pañcamîyaṃ vidyaitābhiḥ abhimantrya jyotir-mayaṃ tad arghyaṃ vidhāya || Parks_3.30 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vāgbhava</s> (the seed of speech), speak, speak! Then, O goddess of eloquence, O you who are moist with the intoxication of speech, O moistener, moisten! Cause great agitation, the pair of <s>Mādana</s> (intoxication), [and] <s>Śakti</s> (power) — cause liberation, cause liberation! The sound is the aggregate of ha-sa-fourteen-fifteen, and the aggregate of sa-ha-fourteen-sixteen — this is the fifth <s>vidyā</s> (mantra). Having consecrated [the offering] with these [five mantras], one should make that <s>arghya</s> (offering) radiant with light. || Parks_3.30 ||

children.text: tad-bindubhis triśaḥ śirasi guru-pādukām iṣṭvā ārdraṃ jvalati jyotir aham asmi jyotir jvalati brahmâham asmi yo 'ham asmi brahmâham asmi aham asmi brahmâham asmi aham evâhaṃ māṃ juhomi svāheti tad bindum ātmanaḥ kuṇḍalinyāṃ juhuyāt || Parks_3.31 ||
children.translated_text: With drops of that [consecrated water], three times on the head, having worshipped the <s>guru-pādukā</s> (the sandals of the teacher): 'The moist one blazes; I am the light; the light blazes; I am <s>Brahman</s>; what I am, that is <s>Brahman</s>; I am <s>Brahman</s>; I am; I am <s>Brahman</s>; I alone am; I offer myself [as oblation], <s>svāhā</s>' — one should offer that <s>bindu</s> (drop) of the self into the <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>. || Parks_3.31 ||

children.text: etad arghya-śodhanam iti śivam || Parks_3.32 ||
children.translated_text: This is the purification of the <s>arghya</s> (offering). Thus [ends the section]. Auspiciousness. || Parks_3.32 ||

children.text: 4. Khaṇḍa: Lalitā-krama
children.translated_text: Chapter 4: The Sequence of <s>Lalitā</s>

children.text: atha hṛc-cakra-sthitām antas-suṣumṇā-padmâṭavī-nirbhedana-kuśalāṃ nirasta-moha-timirāṃ śiva-dīpa-dīptim ādyāṃ saṃvidaṃ vahan-nāsa-puṭena nirgamayya līlā-''kalita-vapuṣaṃ tāṃ trikhaṇḍa-mudrā-śikhaṇḍe kusumâñjalau haste samānīya || Parks_4.1 ||
children.translated_text: Now, carrying the primal <s>Saṃvid</s> (consciousness), who abides in the <s>cakra</s> (wheel) of the heart, who is skilled in piercing through the lotus-groves of the inner <s>Suṣumṇā</s> (central channel), from whom the darkness of delusion is dispelled, who shines with the light of <s>Śiva</s>, bringing her out through the right nostril, [and perceiving] her who has assumed a form through divine play, one should bring her into the hands in a flower-offering held in the <s>Trikhaṇḍa-mudrā</s> (three-section seal gesture). || Parks_4.1 ||

children.text: māyā-lakṣmī parā uccārya devī-nāma câmṛta-caitanya-mūrtiṃ kalpayāmi namaḥ - iti kalpayitvā || Parks_4.2 ||
children.translated_text: Having uttered '<s>Māyā</s>, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Parā</s>' and the name of the <s>Devī</s> (Goddess), 'I fashion [her as] the immortal, conscious form, salutation' — thus having fashioned [her]. || Parks_4.2 ||

children.text: ha-sa-ra-yujaṃ vācaṃ ha-sa-yuktāṃ ka-la-rīṃ ha-sa-ra-caturdaśa-ṣoḍaśān apy uccārya,
children.translated_text: Having uttered the speech-syllable joined with ha-sa-ra, ka-la-rīṃ joined with ha-sa, and ha-sa-ra-fourteen-sixteen,

children.text: mahā-padma-vanântaḥsthe kāraṇânanda-vigrahe |
children.translated_text: O you who dwell within the great lotus-forest, whose form is the bliss of the ultimate cause,

children.text: sarva-bhūta-hite mātar ehy ehi parameśvari ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Mother</s>, who are devoted to the welfare of all beings, come, come, O supreme sovereign!

children.text: iti baindava-cakre para-citim āvāhya || Parks_4.3 ||
children.translated_text: Thus one should invoke the supreme consciousness in the <s>Baindava-cakra</s> (the central point of the <s>Śrī Cakra</s>). || Parks_4.3 ||

children.text: catuṣṣaṣṭy-upacārān kuryāt | sarve upacāra-mantrāḥ tritārī-pūrvāḥ kalpayāmi namaḥ - ity antāḥ kartavyāḥ || Parks_4.4 ||
children.translated_text: One should perform the sixty-four <s>upacāras</s> (modes of worship). All <s>upacāra</s> (worship) <s>mantras</s> should begin with the triple tārī and end with 'I fashion [this], salutation.' || Parks_4.4 ||

children.text: tritārīm uccārya pādyaṃ kalpayāmi namaḥ iti krameṇa ābharaṇâvaropaṇaṃ sugandhi-tailâbhyaṅgaṃ majjana-śālā-praveśanaṃ majjana-maṇḍapa-maṇi-pīṭhopaveśanaṃ divya-snānīyodvartanam uṣṇodaka-snānam kanaka-kalaśa-cyuta-sakala-tīrthâbhi- [139] ṣekaṃ dhauta-vastra-parimārjanam aruṇa-dukūla-paridhānam aruṇa-kucottarīyam ālepa-maṇḍapa-praveśanam ālepa-maṇḍapa-maṇi-pīṭhopaveśanaṃ candanâgaru-kuṅkuma-saṅku-mṛgamada-karpūra-kastūrī-gorocanâdi-divya-gandha-sarvâṅgīṇa-vilepanaṃ keśa-bharasya kālâgaru-dhūpaṃ mallikā-mālatī-jātī-campakâśoka-śatapatra-pūga-kuḍmalī-punnāga-kalhāra-mukhya-sarva-rtu-kusuma-mālāṃ bhūṣaṇa-maṇḍapa-praveśanaṃ bhūṣaṇa-maṇḍapa-maṇi-pīṭhopaveśanaṃ nava-maṇi-makuṭaṃ candra-śakalaṃ sīmanta-sindūraṃ tilaka-ratnaṃ kālâñjanaṃ pālī-yugalaṃ maṇi-kuṇḍala-yugalaṃ nāsâbharaṇam adhara-yāvakaṃ prathama-bhūṣaṇaṃ kanaka-cintākaṃ padakaṃ mahāpadakaṃ muktâvalim ekâvaliṃ channa-vīraṃ keyūra-yugala-catuṣṭayaṃ valayâvalim ūrmikâvaliṃ kāñcī-dāma-kaṭi-sūtraṃ saubhāgyâbharaṇaṃ pāda-kaṭakaṃ ratna-nūpuraṃ pādâṅgulīyakam eka-kare pāśam anya-kare aṅkuśam itara-kare puṇḍrekṣu-cāpam apara-kare puṣpa-bāṇān śrīman-māṇikya-pāduke svasamāna-veṣābhir āvaraṇa-devatābhiḥ saha mahā-cakrâdhirohaṇaṃ kāmeśvarâṅka-paryaṅkopaveśanam amṛtâsava-caṣakam ācamanīyaṃ karpūra-vīṭikām ānandollāsa-vilāsa-hāsaṃ maṅgalârārtikaṃ chatraṃ cāmara-yugalaṃ darpaṇaṃ tāla-vṛntaṃ gandhaṃ puṣpaṃ dhūpaṃ dīpaṃ naivedyaṃ kalpayāmi namaḥ - iti catuṣṣaṣṭy-upacārān vidhāya || Parks_4.5 ||
children.translated_text: Having uttered the <s>Tārī</s> thrice, saying 'I offer the foot-wash, <s>namaḥ</s>,' one should perform in sequence: the removal of ornaments, anointing with fragrant oil, entering the bathing hall, seating upon a jeweled pedestal in the bathing pavilion, rubbing with divine bathing unguents, bathing with hot water, anointing with all sacred waters flowing from a golden pitcher, wiping with washed cloth, donning a red silk garment, a red breast-cloth, entering the unguent pavilion, seating upon a jeweled pedestal in the unguent pavilion, anointing the entire body with divine fragrances of sandal, aloe, saffron, musk-deer scent, camphor, <s>kastūrī</s>, <s>gorocanā</s> and the like, fumigating the hair with black aloe incense, garlands of jasmine, <s>mālatī</s>, <s>jātī</s>, <s>campaka</s>, <s>aśoka</s>, hundred-petaled lotus, areca-bud, <s>punnāga</s>, and <s>kalhāra</s> — chief flowers of all seasons, entering the ornament pavilion, seating upon a jeweled pedestal therein, a crown of nine jewels, a crescent moon, vermillion at the parting, a jeweled <s>tilaka</s>, black collyrium, a pair of ear-ornaments, a pair of jeweled earrings, a nose-ornament, red lac on the lips, the first ornament, a golden <s>cintāka</s>, a pendant, a great pendant, a pearl necklace, a single-strand necklace, a <s>channavīra</s>, four pairs of armlets, a row of bangles, a row of rings, a golden girdle-cord and waist-thread, an auspicious ornament, ankle bracelets, jeweled anklets, toe-rings; in one hand the noose, in another the goad, in the third the sugarcane bow, in the fourth the flower arrows; the glorious ruby sandals; with attendant deities of the enclosures dressed in matching attire — the ascent to the great <s>cakra</s>, seating upon the lap of <s>Kāmeśvara</s>, a cup of the nectar-wine, mouth-rinsing water, a camphor <s>vīṭikā</s> (betel), a blissful joyous playful smile, the auspicious <s>ārārtika</s> (waving of lights), a parasol, a pair of <s>cāmaras</s> (whisks), a mirror, a palm-leaf fan, perfume, flowers, incense, a lamp, and food-offering — saying 'I offer, <s>namaḥ</s>' — thus performing the sixty-four services.

children.text: nava-mudrāś ca pradarśya || Parks_4.6 ||
children.translated_text: And displaying the nine <s>mudrās</s>.

children.text: mūlena tridhā santarpya || Parks_4.7 ||
children.translated_text: Satisfying thrice with the root <s>mantra</s>.

children.text: devyā agnîśâsura-vāyuṣu madhye dikṣu ca ṣaḍ-aṅgāni pūjayitvā || Parks_4.8 ||
children.translated_text: Having worshiped the six limbs (<s>ṣaḍaṅga</s>) of the <s>Devī</s> in the fire, <s>Īśa</s>, <s>asura</s>, and wind quarters, in the center and in the directions.

children.text: vāk-sa-ka-la-hrīṃ nitya-klinne mada-drave sauḥ - iti kāmeśvarī | sarvatra nityā-śrī-pāduketi yojyam | vāg-bhaga-bhuge bhagini bhagodari bhaga-māle bhagâvahe bhaga-guhye bhaga-yoni bhaga-nipātini sarva-bhaga-vaśaṅkari bhaga-rūpe nitya-klinne bhaga-svarūpe sarvāṇi bhagāni me hy ānaya vara-de rete surete bhaga-klinne klinna-drave kledaya drāvaya amoghe bhaga-vicce kṣubha kṣobhaya sarva-sa- [147] ttvān bhageśvari aiṃ blūṃ jeṃ blūṃ bheṃ blūṃ moṃ blūṃ heṃ blūṃ heṃ klinne sarvāṇi bhagāni me vaśam ānaya strīṃ hara bleṃ hrīṃ bhaga-mālinī | tāro māyā nitya-klinne mada-drave svāhā - iti nitya-klinnā | praṇavaḥ kroṃ bhroṃ krauṃ jhrauṃ chrauṃ jrauṃ svāhā - iti bheruṇḍā | praṇavo māyā vahni-vāsinyai namaḥ - iti vahni-vāsinī | māyā-klinne vāk kroṃ nitya-mada-drave hrīṃ - iti mahā-vajreśvarī | māyā śiva-dūtyai namaḥ - iti śiva-dūtī | praṇavo māyā huṃ khe ca che kṣaḥ strīṃ huṃ kṣeṃ hrīṃ phaṭ - iti tvaritā | kumārī kula-sundarī | ha-sa-ka-la-ra-ḍa-vāgbhava-ha-sa-ka-la-ra-ḍa-bindu-mālinī-ha-sa-ka-la-ra-ḍa-caturdaśa-ṣoḍaśā - iti nityā | māyā phreṃ srūṃ aṅkuśa-pāśa-smara-vāgbhava-blūṃ-pada-nitya-mada-drave varma phreṃ māyeti nīla-patākā | bha-ma-ra-ya-ūm iti vijayā | svaum iti sarva-maṅgalā | tāro namo bhagavati jvālā-mālini deva-devi sarva-bhūta-saṃhāra-kārike jāta-vedasi jvalanti jvala jvala prajvala prajvala tri-jāti-yukta-māyā-repha-saptaka-jvālā-mālini varma-phaḍ-agni-jāyeti jvālā-mālinī | (aṃ) ckauṃ - iti citreti pañcadaśa nityāḥ prathama-try-asra-rekhā-sthita-pañcadaśa-svareṣu pūjyaḥ | visṛṣṭau ṣoḍaśīṃ mūla-vidyayā câbhyarcya || Parks_4.9 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vāk-sa-ka-la-hrīṃ nityaklinne madadrave sauḥ</s> — thus <s>Kāmeśvarī</s>. Everywhere '<s>Nityā-śrī-pāduka</s>' should be added. [Then the mantras of the fifteen <s>Nityā</s> deities are given:] <s>Nityaklinnā</s>, <s>Bheruṇḍā</s>, <s>Vahnivāsinī</s>, <s>Mahāvajreśvarī</s>, <s>Śivadūtī</s>, <s>Tvaritā</s>, <s>Kulasundarī</s>, <s>Nityā</s>, <s>Nīlapatākā</s>, <s>Vijayā</s>, <s>Sarvamaṅgalā</s>, <s>Jvālāmālinī</s>, and <s>Citrā</s> — these fifteen <s>Nityā</s> deities are to be worshiped on the fifteen vowels situated on the line of the first triangle. At the end, one should worship the sixteenth with the root <s>vidyā</s>.

children.text: madhye prāk-tryasram adhyāntaḥ muni-veda-nāga-saṅkhyān yathā-sampradāyaṃ pādukān divya-siddha-mānavaugha-siddhān iṣṭvā paścāt sva-śirasi nāthaṃ yajet | etal-layâṅga-pūjanam - iti śivam || Parks_4.10 ||
children.translated_text: In the center, before the triangle, inward, one should worship the <s>pādukas</s> (sacred sandals) — of the sages, <s>Vedas</s>, and <s>Nāgas</s> in number — according to tradition, belonging to the divine, <s>siddha</s>, and human lineages of adepts. Afterward, one should worship the Lord upon one's own head. This is the worship of the limb of dissolution (<s>layāṅga</s>) — thus ends auspiciously.

children.text: 5. Khaṇḍa: Lalitā-navâvaraṇa-pūjā
children.translated_text: 5. Section: The Worship of the Nine Enclosures of <s>Lalitā</s> (<s>Lalitā-navāvaraṇa-pūjā</s>)

children.text: atha prāthamike catur-asre aṇimā-laghimā-mahimeśitva-vaśitva-prākāmya-bhuktîcchā-prāpti-sarvakāma-siddhy-antāḥ madhyame catur-asre brāhmy-ādyā-mahālakṣmy-antāḥ tṛtīye catur-asre saṃkṣobhaṇa-drāvaṇa-karṣaṇa-vaśyonmādana-mahâṅkuśa-khecarī-bīja-yoni-trikhaṇḍāḥ sarva-pūrvās tāḥ sampūjyāḥ || Parks_5.1 ||
children.translated_text: Now, in the first square: <s>Aṇimā</s>, <s>Laghimā</s>, <s>Mahimā</s>, <s>Īśitva</s>, <s>Vaśitva</s>, <s>Prākāmya</s>, <s>Bhukti</s>, <s>Icchā</s>, <s>Prāpti</s>, ending with <s>Sarvakāmasiddhi</s>. In the middle square: from <s>Brāhmī</s> to <s>Mahālakṣmī</s>. In the third square: <s>Saṃkṣobhaṇa</s>, <s>Drāvaṇa</s>, <s>Karṣaṇa</s>, <s>Vaśya</s>, <s>Unmādana</s>, <s>Mahāṅkuśa</s>, <s>Khecarī</s>, <s>Bīja</s>, <s>Yoni</s>, and <s>Trikhaṇḍā</s> — all preceded by 'Sarva' — these should be worshiped.

children.text: etāḥ prakaṭa-yoginyas trailokya-mohana-cakre sa-mudrāḥ sa-siddhayaḥ sâyudhāḥ sa-śaktayaḥ sa-vāhanāḥ sa-parivārāḥ sarvopacāraiḥ sampūjitāḥ santv iti tāsām eva samaṣṭy-arcanaṃ kṛtvā || Parks_5.2 ||
children.translated_text: These are the Manifest <s>Yoginīs</s> (<s>prakaṭayoginī</s>) in the <s>Trailokyamohana</s> (World-Enchanting) <s>Cakra</s>. They should be worshiped with all services, together with their <s>mudrās</s>, <s>siddhis</s>, weapons, <s>śaktis</s>, vehicles, and retinues — performing the collective worship of them all.

children.text: kara-śuddhim uccārya tripurācakreśvarīm avamṛśya drām iti sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇī-mudrāṃ pradarśayet | cakra-yoginī-cakreśīnāṃ nāmāni bhinnāni | śiṣṭaṃ samānam || Parks_5.3 ||
children.translated_text: Having uttered the purification of the hands, meditating upon <s>Tripurā Cakreśvarī</s>, one should display the <s>Sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇī</s> (All-Agitating) <s>mudrā</s> with '<s>drāṃ</s>.' The names of the <s>Cakra-yoginīs</s> and <s>Cakreśīs</s> differ. The rest is the same.

children.text: ṣoḍaśa-patre kāmâkarṣiṇī nityā-kaleti nityā-kalā-'ntāḥ buddhy-ākarṣiṇī-ahaṅkārâkarṣiṇī-śabdâkarṣiṇī-sparśâkarṣiṇī-rūpâkarṣiṇī-rasâkarṣiṇī-gandhâkarṣiṇī-cittâkarṣiṇī-dhairyâkarṣiṇī-smṛty-ākarṣiṇī-nāmâkarṣiṇī-bījâkarṣiṇī-ātmâkarṣiṇī-amṛtâkarṣiṇī-śarīrâkarṣiṇī etā gupta-yoginyaḥ sarvâśā-paripūrake cakre sa-mudrāḥ ity ādi pūrva-vat ātma-rakṣām uccārya tripureśīm iṣṭvā drīṃ - iti sarvavidrāviṇīṃ pradarśayet || Parks_5.4 ||
children.translated_text: On the sixteen petals: <s>Kāmākarṣiṇī</s>, also called <s>Nityākalā</s>, ending with <s>Nityākalā</s> — <s>Buddhyākarṣiṇī</s>, <s>Ahaṅkārākarṣiṇī</s>, <s>Śabdākarṣiṇī</s>, <s>Sparśākarṣiṇī</s>, <s>Rūpākarṣiṇī</s>, <s>Rasākarṣiṇī</s>, <s>Gandhākarṣiṇī</s>, <s>Cittākarṣiṇī</s>, <s>Dhairyākarṣiṇī</s>, <s>Smṛtyākarṣiṇī</s>, <s>Nāmākarṣiṇī</s>, <s>Bījākarṣiṇī</s>, <s>Ātmākarṣiṇī</s>, <s>Amṛtākarṣiṇī</s>, and <s>Śarīrākarṣiṇī</s>. These are the Hidden <s>Yoginīs</s> (<s>guptayoginī</s>) in the <s>Sarvāśāparipūraka</s> (All-Wish-Fulfilling) <s>Cakra</s>, with <s>mudrās</s> etc. as before. Having uttered the self-protection, worshiping <s>Tripureśī</s>, one should display the <s>Sarvavidrāviṇī</s> (All-Melting) <s>mudrā</s> with '<s>drīṃ</s>.'

children.text: dik-patre kusumā-mekhalā-madanā-madanâturā-rekhā-veginy-aṅkuśā-mālinīr anaṅga-pūrvāḥ saṃmṛśyaitā guptatara-yoginyaḥ sarva-saṃkṣobhaṇa-cakre sa-mudrāḥ ity ādi pūrva-vad ātmâsanam uccārya tripurasundarīm iṣṭvā klīm iti sarvâkarṣiṇī-mudrāṃ pradarśayet || Parks_5.5 ||
children.translated_text: On the directional petals: <s>Kusumā</s>, <s>Mekhalā</s>, <s>Madanā</s>, <s>Madanāturā</s>, <s>Rekhā</s>, <s>Veginī</s>, <s>Aṅkuśā</s>, and <s>Mālinī</s> — all preceded by '<s>Anaṅga</s>.' Meditating upon these, the Most Hidden <s>Yoginīs</s> (<s>guptatarayoginī</s>) in the <s>Sarvasaṃkṣobhaṇa</s> (All-Agitating) <s>Cakra</s>, with <s>mudrās</s> etc. as before — having uttered the self-seat, worshiping <s>Tripurasundarī</s>, one should display the <s>Sarvākarṣiṇī</s> (All-Attracting) <s>mudrā</s> with '<s>klīṃ</s>.'

children.text: bhuvanâre saṃkṣobhiṇī-drāviṇy-ākarṣiṇy-āhlādinī-saṃmohinī-stambhinī-jṛmbhiṇī-vaśaṅkarī-rañjany-unmādiny-arthasādhinī-sampattipūraṇī-mantramayī-dvandva-kṣayaṅkarīḥ sarvâdīr avamṛśyaitāḥ sampradāya-yoginyaḥ sarvasaubhāgya- [158] dāyaka-cakre sa-mudrāḥ - ity ādi mantra-śeṣaḥ cakrâsanam uccārya tripuravāsinīṃ cakreśvarīm iṣṭvā blūṃ - iti sarvavaśaṅkarī-mudrām udghāṭayet || Parks_5.6 ||
children.translated_text: On the world-spokes (<s>bhuvanāra</s>): <s>Saṃkṣobhiṇī</s>, <s>Drāviṇī</s>, <s>Ākarṣiṇī</s>, <s>Āhlādinī</s>, <s>Saṃmohinī</s>, <s>Stambhinī</s>, <s>Jṛmbhiṇī</s>, <s>Vaśaṅkarī</s>, <s>Rañjanī</s>, <s>Unmādinī</s>, <s>Arthasādhinī</s>, <s>Sampattipūraṇī</s>, <s>Mantramayī</s>, and <s>Dvandvakṣayaṅkarī</s> — all preceded by 'Sarva.' Meditating upon these, the Tradition <s>Yoginīs</s> (<s>sampradāyayoginī</s>) in the <s>Sarvasaubhāgyadāyaka</s> (All-Fortune-Giving) <s>Cakra</s>, with <s>mudrās</s> etc. — completing the <s>mantra</s>, having uttered the <s>cakra</s>-seat, worshiping <s>Tripuravāsinī</s> as <s>Cakreśvarī</s>, one should display the <s>Sarvavaśaṅkarī</s> (All-Subjugating) <s>mudrā</s> with '<s>blūṃ</s>.'

children.text: bahir-daśâre siddhipradā-sampatpradā-priyaṅkarī-maṅgalakāriṇī-kāmapradā-duḥkhavimocinī-mṛtyupraśamanī-vighnanivāriṇy-aṅgasundarī-saubhāgyadāyinīḥ sarva-pūrvāḥ sampūjyaitāḥ kulottīrṇa-yoginyaḥ sarvârthasādhaka-cakre manu-śeṣam uktvā mantrâsanam uccārya tripurāśrīcakreśvarīṃ pratyavamṛśya sa ity unmādinī-mudrāṃ dadyāt || Parks_5.7 ||
children.translated_text: On the outer ten spokes: <s>Siddhipradā</s>, <s>Sampatpradā</s>, <s>Priyaṅkarī</s>, <s>Maṅgalakāriṇī</s>, <s>Kāmapradā</s>, <s>Duḥkhavimocinī</s>, <s>Mṛtyupraśamanī</s>, <s>Vighnanivāriṇī</s>, <s>Aṅgasundarī</s>, and <s>Saubhāgyadāyinī</s> — all preceded by 'Sarva.' Having worshiped these, the <s>Kulottīrṇa Yoginīs</s> (Beyond-the-Family) in the <s>Sarvārthasādhaka</s> (All-Purpose-Accomplishing) <s>Cakra</s>. Having completed the <s>mantra</s> and uttered the <s>mantra</s>-seat, meditating upon <s>Tripurāśrī Cakreśvarī</s>, one should give the <s>Unmādinī</s> (Maddening) <s>mudrā</s> with '<s>sa</s>.'

children.text: antar-daśâre jñāna-śakty-aiśvaryapradā-jñānamayī-vyādhivināśiny-ādhārasvarūpā-pāpaharā-''nandamayī-rakṣāsvarūpiṇī-psitaphalapradāḥ sarvopapadāḥ [159] yaṣṭavyā etāni garbha-yoginyaḥ sarvarakṣākara-cakre śiṣṭaṃ tad-vat sādhyasiddhâsanam uccārya tripuramālinī mānyā krom iti sarvamahâṅkuśāṃ darśayet || Parks_5.8 ||
children.translated_text: On the inner ten spokes: <s>Jñāna</s>-<s>śakti</s>-<s>aiśvaryapradā</s> (Granter of Knowledge, Power, and Sovereignty), <s>Jñānamayī</s> (Consisting of Knowledge), <s>Vyādhivināśinī</s> (Destroyer of Disease), <s>Ādhārasvarūpā</s> (Of the Nature of Support), <s>Pāpaharā</s> (Remover of Sin), <s>Ānandamayī</s> (Consisting of Bliss), <s>Rakṣāsvarūpiṇī</s> (Of the Nature of Protection), and <s>Psitaphalapradā</s> (Granter of Desired Fruits) — all preceded by 'Sarva.' These should be worshiped. These are the Womb <s>Yoginīs</s> (<s>garbhayoginī</s>) in the <s>Sarvarakṣākara</s> (All-Protecting) <s>Cakra</s>. The rest is likewise. Having uttered the <s>sādhyasiddha</s>-seat, worshiping <s>Tripuramālinī</s>, one should display the <s>Sarvamahāṅkuśā</s> (Great All-Goad) with '<s>kroṃ</s>.'

children.text: aṣṭâre vaśiny-ādy-aṣṭakaṃ namaḥ-sthāne pūjā-mantra-sannāma etā rahasya-yoginyaḥ sarvarogahara-cakre śiṣṭaṃ spaṣṭaṃ mūrti-vidyām uccārya tripurāsiddhām ārādhya śiva-bhṛgu-ṛddhi-yuk-phreṃ - iti khecarī deyā || Parks_5.9 ||
children.translated_text: On the eight spokes: the group of eight beginning with <s>Vaśinī</s>, with '<s>namaḥ</s>' in place of worship-<s>mantra</s> and salutation-name. These are the Secret <s>Yoginīs</s> (<s>rahasyayoginī</s>) in the <s>Sarvarogahara</s> (All-Disease-Removing) <s>Cakra</s>. The rest is clear. Having uttered the <s>mūrti-vidyā</s>, worshiping <s>Tripurāsiddhā</s>, one should give the <s>Khecarī</s> <s>mudrā</s> with '<s>Śiva-bhṛgu-ṛddhi-yuk-phreṃ</s>.'

children.text: bāṇa-bījāny uccārya sarva-jṛmbhaṇebhyo bāṇebhyo namaḥ dhaṃ thaṃ sarva-saṃmohanāya dhanuṣe āṃ hrīṃ sarva-vaśīkaraṇāya pāśāya kroṃ sarva-sthambhanāyâṅkuśāya namaḥ iti mahā-try-asra-bāhya-catur-dikṣu bāṇâdy-āyudha-pūjā || Parks_5.10 ||
children.translated_text: Uttering the arrow-seed syllables, 'Homage to all-expanding arrows, to the bow of all-enchantment dhaṃ thaṃ, to the noose of all-subjugation āṃ hrīṃ, to the goad of all-paralysis kroṃ, namaḥ' — thus the worship of the weapons beginning with the arrows in the four directions outside the great triangle.

children.text: tri-koṇe vāk-kāma-śakti-samasta-pūrvāḥ kāmeśvarī-vajreśvarī-bhagamālinī-mahā-devyaḥ bindau caturthī || Parks_5.11 ||
children.translated_text: In the triangle, preceded by the totality of <s>Vāk</s> (Speech), <s>Kāma</s> (Desire), and <s>Śakti</s> (Power), are the great goddesses <s>Kāmeśvarī</s>, <s>Vajreśvarī</s>, and <s>Bhagamālinī</s>; the fourth is at the <s>bindu</s> (point).

children.text: tisṛṇām āsām anantaram abhedāya mūla-devyāḥ pūjā | kāmeśvary-ādi-caturthī nityānāṃ ṣoḍaśī cakra-devīnāṃ navamī bindu-cakra-sthā cety ekaiva | na tatra mantra-devatā-bhedaḥ kāryaḥ | tan-mahā-devyā eva | caturṣu sthaleṣu viśeṣârcanam āvartate || Parks_5.12 ||
children.translated_text: After these three, for the sake of non-difference, the worship of the root goddess. The fourth of [those beginning with] <s>Kāmeśvarī</s>, the sixteenth of the <s>Nityās</s>, and the ninth of the <s>cakra</s> deities situated in the <s>bindu-cakra</s> — all these are one and the same. No distinction of <s>mantra</s> and deity should be made there. They are all of that Great Goddess alone. Special worship recurs in four places.

children.text: etā atirahasya-yoginyaḥ sarvasiddhiprade cakre | pariśiṣṭaṃ draṣṭavyam | āvāhanīm uccārya tripurâmbāṃ sambhāvya hsauṃ - iti bīja-mudrā-kṛtiḥ || Parks_5.13 ||
children.translated_text: These are the Most Secret <s>Yoginīs</s> (<s>atirahasya-yoginī</s>) in the <s>Sarvasiddhiprada</s> (All-Perfection-Granting) <s>Cakra</s>. The remainder should be seen [in the appendix]. Uttering the invocation [mantra], receiving <s>Tripurāmbā</s>, 'hsauṃ' — thus the <s>bīja-mudrā</s> (seed-gesture) is formed.

children.text: bindu-cakre mūlena devīm iṣṭvā eṣā parâpara-rahasya-yoginī sarvânandamaye cakre sa-mudrā sa-siddhiḥ sâyudhā sa-śaktiḥ sa-vāhanā sa-parivārā sarvopacāraiḥ saṃpūjitā 'stv iti punar mūlam uccārya, mahācakreśvarīm iṣṭvā vāgbhavena yoniṃ pradarśya || Parks_5.14 ||
children.translated_text: Having worshipped the <s>Devī</s> at the <s>bindu-cakra</s> with the root mantra — she is the Supreme-and-Lesser Secret <s>Yoginī</s> (<s>parāpara-rahasya-yoginī</s>) in the <s>Sarvānandamaya</s> (All-Bliss-Consisting) <s>Cakra</s>, with <s>mudrā</s>, with <s>siddhi</s>, with weapons, with <s>śakti</s>, with vehicle, with retinue, 'may she be worshipped with all services' — again uttering the root mantra, having worshipped <s>Mahācakreśvarī</s>, displaying the <s>yoni</s> (source) [mudrā] with <s>Vāgbhava</s>.

children.text: pūrva-vad dhūpa-dīpa-mudrā-tarpaṇa-naivedyâdi dattvā || Parks_5.15 ||
children.translated_text: As before, offering incense, lamp, <s>mudrā</s>, <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation), <s>naivedya</s> (food offering), etc.

children.text: bindunā mukhaṃ bindu-dvayena kucau sa-parârdhena yoniṃ kṛtvā kāma-kalām iti dhyātvā || Parks_5.16 ||
children.translated_text: Making the mouth with the <s>bindu</s>, the breasts with two <s>bindus</s>, and the <s>yoni</s> with the half-and-superior [portion] — thus meditating on the <s>kāma-kalā</s> (the erotic syllable).

children.text: saubhāgya-hṛdayam āmṛśya || Parks_5.17 ||
children.translated_text: Touching the <s>Saubhāgya-hṛdaya</s> (Heart of Auspiciousness) [mantra].

children.text: vāma-bhāga-vihita-tri-koṇa-vṛtta-catur-asre gandhâkṣatârcite vāgbhavam uccārya vyāpaka-maṇḍalāya namaḥ ity ardha-bhakta-bharitâmbhasā ādimopādima-madhyama-bhājanaṃ tatra nyasya || Parks_5.18 ||
children.translated_text: In a triangle-circle-square arrangement placed to the left, worshipped with sandalwood paste and unbroken rice, uttering <s>Vāgbhava</s>, 'Homage to the all-pervading <s>maṇḍala</s>' — placing vessels of the first, last, and middle [portions] filled with half-eaten food and water therein.

children.text: praṇava-māyā-'nte sarva-vighna-kṛdbhyaḥ sarva-bhūtebhyo huṃ svāhā - iti triḥ paṭhitvā baliṃ dattvā || Parks_5.19 ||
children.translated_text: Reciting three times 'to all obstacle-makers, to all beings, huṃ svāhā' after <s>praṇava</s> and <s>māyā</s>, and giving the <s>bali</s> (offering).

children.text: pradakṣiṇa-namaskāra-japa-stotraiḥ santoṣya || Parks_5.20 ||
children.translated_text: Satisfying [the deities] with circumambulation, prostrations, <s>japa</s> (mantra recitation), and <s>stotras</s> (hymns of praise).

children.text: tad-rūpiṇīm ekāṃ śaktiṃ bālayopacāraiḥ sampūjya tāṃ ma-pañcakena santarpya || Parks_5.21 ||
children.translated_text: Worshipping one <s>śakti</s> in her form with the services of a young girl, and satisfying her with the <s>ma-pañcaka</s> (five substances beginning with 'ma').

children.text: śiṣṭaiḥ sārdhaṃ cid-agnau haviś-śeṣaṃ hutvā || Parks_5.22 ||
children.translated_text: Together with the adepts, offering the remainder of the oblation into the fire of consciousness.

children.text: khecarīṃ baddhvā kṣamasveti visṛjya tām ātmani saṃyojayet iti śivam || Parks_5.23 ||
children.translated_text: Binding the <s>Khecarī</s> [mudrā], bidding farewell with 'forgive me,' one should unite her into oneself. Thus, auspiciousness.

children.text: 6. Khaṇḍa: Śyāmā-krama
children.translated_text: Chapter 6: <s>Śyāmā-krama</s> (The Procedure of Śyāmā)

children.text: iyam eva mahatī vidyā siṃhâsaneśvarī sāmrājñī, tasyāḥ pradhāna-saciva-padaṃ śyāmā, tat-krama-vimṛṣṭiḥ sadā kāryā || Parks_6.1 ||
children.translated_text: This very great <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge/mantra) is the empress enthroned upon the lion-seat; <s>Śyāmā</s> holds the position of chief minister to her. Reflection upon her procedure should always be practiced.

children.text: pradhāna-dvārā rāja-prasādanaṃ hi nyāyyam || Parks_6.2 ||
children.translated_text: For it is proper to please the sovereign through the chief minister.

children.text: brāhme muhūrte cotthāya śayane sthitvaiva śrī-pādukāṃ praṇamya prāṇān āyamya mūlâdi-dvādaśânta-paryantaṃ jvalantīṃ para-saṃvidaṃ vicintya manasā mūlaṃ triśo japtvā bahir nirgatya vimukta-mala-mūtro danta-dhāvana-jihvā-gharṣaṇa-kapha-vimocana-nāsa-śodhana-viṃśati-gaṇḍūṣān vidhāya || Parks_6.3 ||
children.translated_text: Rising at the <s>brahma-muhūrta</s> (pre-dawn hour) and remaining on the bed itself, bowing to the sacred <s>śrī-pādukā</s> (guru's sandals), restraining the breath, meditating upon the blazing supreme consciousness from the root to the end of the <s>dvādaśānta</s> (twelve-finger space above the head), mentally reciting the root mantra three times, then going outside, having relieved oneself, performing tooth-cleaning, tongue-scraping, phlegm-removal, nose-cleansing, and twenty gargles.

children.text: mantra-bhasma-jala-snāneṣv iṣṭaṃ vidhāya vastraṃ paridhāya || Parks_6.4 ||
children.translated_text: Performing the desired [practice] among bathing with mantra-consecrated ash and water, and putting on garments.

children.text: sandhyām upāsya savitṛ-maṇḍale devīṃ sâvaraṇaṃ vicintya mūlena trir arghyaṃ dattvā yathā-śakti santarpya || Parks_6.5 ||
children.translated_text: Performing the <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight worship), meditating upon the <s>Devī</s> with her enclosure in the orb of <s>Savitṛ</s> (the Sun), giving <s>arghya</s> three times with the root mantra, and satisfying [the deity] according to one's ability.

children.text: yāga-gṛhaṃ praviśyâsane ādhāra-śakti-kamalâsanāya nama - ity upaviśya || Parks_6.6 ||
children.translated_text: Entering the worship hall and sitting on the seat with 'Homage to <s>Ādhāra-Śakti</s> (Foundation Power), to the lotus-seat.'

children.text: samasta-prakaṭa-gupta-siddha-yoginī-cakra-śrī-pādukābhyo nama iti śirasy añjalim ādhāya sva-guru-pādukā-pūjāṃ ca vidhāya || Parks_6.7 ||
children.translated_text: Placing the <s>añjali</s> (joined palms) on the head with 'Homage to the <s>śrī-pādukās</s> of the <s>cakras</s> of all manifest, hidden, and perfected <s>yoginīs</s>,' and performing the worship of one's own <s>guru-pādukā</s> (teacher's sandals).

children.text: aiṃ hraḥ astrāya phaṭ ity astra-mantreṇa aṅguṣṭhâdi-kaniṣṭhântaṃ kara-talayoḥ kūrparayoḥ dehe ca vyāpakatvena vinyasya || Parks_6.8 ||
children.translated_text: With the <s>astra</s> (weapon) mantra 'aiṃ hraḥ astrāya phaṭ,' placing [the mantra] from thumb to little finger, on the palms, elbows, and body in an all-pervading manner.

children.text: yaṃ - iti vāyuṃ piṅgalayā ''kṛṣya deham upaviśoṣya, raṃ - iti vāyum ākṛṣya dehaṃ dagdhvā, vaṃ - iti vāyum ākṛṣyâmṛtena dagdha-deha-bhasma siktvā, laṃ - iti vāyum ākṛṣya dṛḍhaṃ vidhāya, haṃsa - iti vāyum ākṛṣya śiva-caitanyam utpādya || Parks_6.9 ||
children.translated_text: With 'yaṃ' — drawing the wind through the <s>piṅgalā</s> (solar channel), desiccating the body; with 'raṃ' — drawing the fire, burning the body; with 'vaṃ' — drawing the wind, sprinkling the ashes of the burnt body with nectar; with 'laṃ' — drawing the wind, making it firm; with '<s>haṃsa</s>' — drawing the wind, generating the consciousness of <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: mūlam ekaśa uccārya vāyum ākṛṣya triśaḥ uccārya kumbhayitvā sakṛd uccārya recayet | evaṃ recaka-pūraka-kumbhakaṃ tridhā saptadhā daśadhā ṣoḍaśadhā vā viracya tejo-maya-tanuḥ || Parks_6.10 ||
